title: Allow content intents

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
AntennaPod currently only allows `action.VIEW` intents if they contain the data `file://`. File manager and Gallery applications often send a `content://` intent. The `MediaMetadataRetriever` function used in `ExternalMedia` theoretically supports `content://` intents, so all we need to do is to pass the Context to `ExternalMedia`.

It would be nice if I could open any file with AntennaPod, because I like the playback speed option.

**Expected behaviour**: After an episode is removed from the queue, it should be deleted.

**Current behaviour**: I started receiving warnings from the Google app updater, saying I didn't have enough space left on my device to install updates. Using the Android storage analyzer, it found that apps were consuming most of my storage, and that AntennaPod was consuming 10GB by itself. However, this doesn't seem to be the case. And sure enough, in the folders for the podcasts whose episodes I've either listened to or have removed from my queue, there are a ton of files, some dating back months.

Until this bug is fixed, as a workaround, can I delete this entire directory, or will that destroy Antennapod? There seems to be a folder for every podcast I've ever listened to, even ones that I unsubscribed  from and removed from Antennapod. Why is it not deleting those folders?

title: Share podcast / episod with itpc:// protocol prefix
body:
I often share an episode or entire feed friends over WhatsApp etc.

It would be good if when the recipient clicked the link I sent them it opened in their podcast app if they have one.

## The problem

Currently what is sent is (depending on the podcast in question) usually some web page link to a page of varying quality and usefulness, often resulting in the recipient failing to listen to what I send because it's all too much of a pain, or using the embedded webpage player even though they are using a phone that has a podcast listener installed.

## Suggestion

The Share Link button could normalize the feed url to start with `itpc://` before sharing.

It would be good to choose the prefix with the broadest support, I'm not sure what apps support which.

----

Useful info: https://codex.wordpress.org/Podcasting

This is basically the inverse of issue #333

title: Using AlarmManager.set() to set the alarm and update feeds may be delayed
body:
Hi,

I found API [AlarmManager.set()](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/AlarmManager.html#set(int,%20long,%20android.app.PendingIntent)) is used in [UserPreferences.java](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/e884e989c781a2527b737ff30f0fcadd23e791f5/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/preferences/UserPreferences.java) to schedule the alarm to update the feeds automatically at some time.
For your information, from API 19, the alarm scheduled by this API may not be triggered at the exact time you set. It may be delayed due to the system scheduling. So, the update may be delayed.
To have on time alarm scheduling, you may use setExact or setWindow instead.

Thx.

title: Allow setting order (or priority) of podcast to download

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Currently it seems when you use auto download and have free space AntennaPod will download the latest podcast episode from all subscribed podcasts.

I propose to have a mechanism in which you can specify a podcast to look for un-listened episodes for in order to download before looking for the latest episode from all podcasts.

Eg. Say you listen to a number of podcasts, A, B, C
A uploads a new episode at 13.00
B uploads a new episode at 15.00
and C at 20.00

I propose we can somehow make it so that if a has an episode that has not been listened to yet, it gets priority over all other podcasts. (This would mean in order to not download all past episodes the user would need to mark them as listened to)

The way I could see this working is either:
- Each podcast has a priority value, higher values get checked first when auto-downloading a new episode, equal priority podcasts can just use the current deciding factor (latest episode?)
- In the auto-download settings there is a list of all subscribed podcasts, users can re-order the list and when auto downloading a new episode the subscribed podcasts are searched in the order in which they appear in the list

title: Support Android Autobackup for Apps
body:
When my phone broke recently I lost all my Antennapod subscriptions, play lists, downloaded MP3s, etc. despite having backup to my Google Drive turned on. This shouldn't have happened. All Antennapod data should have been backed up to Google drive and restored automatically onto my new phone.

Note that there should be no extra UI to implement this. The UI is all at the Android system settings level. 

see https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/data/autobackup.html for technical details. This may be as simple as adding this to the manifest:

```
<application ...
    android:allowBackup="true">
</app>
```

Storage is limited to 25 MB so you probably can't use it for the MP3s, but that should be more than enough space for all the metadata. 

This is related to but not the same as #377 which requests the Option to export/import database #377. That is a manual export that could be used to move data to a phone with a different account.

title: Allow Audio Playback from Android Audio
body:
AntennaPod is my go-to app for listening in the car.  Unfortunately it doesn't integrate well with Android's automobile technology.  

Instructions for supporting discovery and playback from Android Auto are found [Here](https://developer.android.com/training/auto/audio/index.html).  

#### Requirements

1.  Some labels in the Manifest file
2. A conditional in alarm management to only trigger if not in Car mode

#### Harder Stuff
3. Implement the Queue as a [MediaBrowserService](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/media/MediaBrowserService.html)
4. Enable playback through a [MediaSession](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/session/MediaSession.html)
5. [Allow voice commands to control playback](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xc2HZSwPcwM)

title: Pubdate respecting smart shuffle

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Copied from Google Groups:

Hi, 
 
I love AntennaPod and gave it five stars on the Android App Store. 
 
One feature that I often wish for is a kind of ‘smart shuffle’. I listen to (let’s say) five podcasts, and some of them are episodic, so it’s nice to listen to them in order. Since different podcasts began on different dates, and have a different frequency (e.g. weekly, bi-weekly, etc.), when I add multiple podcasts to my queue and then sort the queue by date, I get something like this: 
 
•    Radiolab 1 
•    Radiolab 2 
•    Radiolab 3 
•        : 
•        : 
•    Radiolab N 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 1 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 2 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 3 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 4 
•    Radiolab N+1 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 5 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 6 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 7 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 8 
•    Radiolab N+2 
•        : 
•        : 
•    Fresh Air 1 
•    Radiolab N+2 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 1 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 2 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 3 
•    Fresh Air 2 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 4 
•    Radiolab N+1 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 5 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 6 
•    Fresh Air 3 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 7 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 8 
•    Radiolab N+2 
•        : 
•        : 
This is correctly sorted according to date, but it can result in ‘clumping’ of podcast episodes; something that’s not as pleasant to listen to. A ‘smart shuffle’ would pick episodes in date order from each subscribed podcast, round-robin fashion. This would result in a queue that looked more like the following: 
 
•    Fresh Air 1 
•    Radiolab 1 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 1 
•    Fresh Air 2 
•    Radiolab 2 
•    Thrilling Adventure Hour 2 
•        : 
•        : 
  
Even though Radiolab episode #1 aired (let’s say) years before Fresh Air episode #1, the important thing is that Radiolab episodes are queued in order and Fresh Air episodes are queued in order. Of course, ‘clumping’ would still occur at the very end of your queue unless you happened to have the same number of episodes from each different podcast. That’s OK, I think, because I usually just add all new episodes from each subscribed podcast to my queue. By the time I’ve burned through a significant percentage of my queue, there are usually new episodes, and I can re-sort to interleave the new episodes.  So, though there may be 'clumps' at the end of the queue, I never actually come close to reaching the end of the queue.
 
I find myself manually arranging my queue this way, and it’s very time-consuming and labor-intensive (even more so on a phone). Perhaps this could be an alternate Sort By choice, like “Date, Ascending (interleaved)”.

title: Feature request: bookmarks by shaking the device
body:
Hi,
I really love AntennaPod and I use it also for listening to conferences, lessons and other speeches while I'm walking, running or driving. 
It would be great if someone can add a simple feature: add a bookmark by shaking the device.

If I'm driving listening a conference, I could want to remember a particular part of the speech but I can't look at the phone or write a note with the minutes:seconds that I am listening to. So a feature could be to shake the phone and AntennaPod "writes" a bookmark with the name of the audio file, the minute and the second. 
It would be much more useful if AntennaPod bookmark the current time minus a custom time set by the user.
E.g. I set the "timer" 30 seconds before the current position. If I'm listening to 14m 52s, when I shake the phone the bookmark should be created on 14m 22s. If I set the timer to 45 seconds, the bookmark goes to 14' 07" and so on.

title: Stream/Delete and Download/Play buttons should not share the same real estate in UI
body:
Because I listen to most podcasts at home with wifi, I use the "Stream" button often. However, occasionally I like to listen to podcasts where there is no network access, and in this case I download episodes in advance. When a podcast has been downloaded, the "Stream" button is replaced with the "Delete" button, and the "Download" button is replaced by the "Play" button. However, muscle memory often takes over and I hit "Delete" when I mean to hit "Stream" (really "Play"), because this is the button I'm used to using.

I find the organisation of the buttons non-intuitive. Perhaps the "Play"/"Stream" buttons could share the same real estate, and the "Delete"/"Download" buttons could share the same real estate. This seems more intuitive, and I expect would lead to less accidental episode deletions.

**Android version**: 7.1.2 LineageOS 14.1

**Devide model**: Nexus 5

**Expected behaviour**: Not accidentally deleting episodes due to muscle memory and placement of the "Stream" and "Delete" buttons.

title: Feed that contains both video and mp3 selects video
body:
# Problem
Specifically this feed has the issue: http://tv.ida.dk/audiopodcast/channel/16944635

I have been debug'ing to find the root of this issue.
It happens while parsing the feed. First it goes through the de.danoeh.antennapod.core.syndication.namespace.NSRSS20 parser which sets the media to a FeedMedia object with the correct download url. Later during the parsing it goes through de.danoeh.antennapod.core.syndication.namespace.NSMedia which in line 95 sets the media to a FeedMedia object with the video url (from the media:content element in the feed).
When it is done parsing it is left with the wrong download url.

This happens because the "isDefault" attribute of the "content" element is "true".

# Possible solution
1. Would it be a solution to not add the FeedMedia object from NSMedia if the "type" attribute of the "content" element were video?
2. Alternatively it could be solved by making it configureable which source from the feed should be used for the download.

I could spent some time working on a fix.
Which solution would be preferred? Solution number 1 would gives the best user experience since the feed will just work. I am just not sure if it will break something else.

title: Split up two different uses of the string "New" into two different strings

labels.name: Good first issue
labels.description: Can be addressed without deep knowledge of the AntennaPod code. But exploring the code may be needed

body:
The string **new_label** (https://www.transifex.com/antennapod/antennapod/translate/#da/$/6971314?q=new) is being used twice, in plural form and in singular form.

It seems like the problem is in \app\src\main\java\de\danoeh\antennapod\fragment\EpisodesFragment.java:

                case POS_ALL_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.all_episodes_short_label);
                case POS_NEW_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.new_label);
                case POS_FAV_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.favorite_episodes_label);

This should be

                case POS_ALL_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.all_episodes_short_label);
                case POS_NEW_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.new_episodes_label);
                case POS_FAV_EPISODES:
                    return resources.getString(R.string.favorite_episodes_label);

and then **new_episodes_label** should be created as a new translatable string, for the plural case, in \core\src\main\res\values\strings.xml:

    <string name="episodes_label">Episodes</string>
    <string name="new_episodes_label">New</string>
    <string name="all_episodes_short_label">All</string>
    <string name="favorite_episodes_label">Favorites</string>
    <string name="new_label">New</string>

**new_label** will then be the badge/label on specific episodes, i.e. the singular case.

I don't have experience with pull requests and all that, so maybe someone with that experience can make the change?

**Edit**: Corrected label_new to new_label; sorry for the confusion.

title: Resume downloads if service was killed
body:
If the download service is killed by Android or a taskmanager, restarting the download creates a second file. The old one stays in the media folder without any reference in the database. 

As suggested by mfietz, the `downloaded` field in the DB should be expanded to allow persisting the state of started downloads.

title: Image loading is in the main thread
body:
Dear developers,
I found some images are loaded in the main thread in AntennaPod.

For image loading, Google says this:
https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/graphics/index.html
" Loading bitmaps on the UI thread can degrade your app's performance, causing slow responsiveness or even ANR messages."

I noticed that in the following code, image loading is in worker thread:
https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/service/playback/PlaybackService.java
de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.playback.PlaybackService.java   run()  (line number: 1159)
(bitmap is loaded with the invocation of decodeResource ())

However, in the code below, image loading is in the main thread: 
https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/service/download/DownloadService.java
(1) de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.download.DownloadService.java   setupNotificationBuilders()   (line number: 340 )
(bitmap is loaded with the invocation of decodeResource ())
which is called by  de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.download.DownloadService.java  onCreate()

(2) de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.download.DownloadService.java  updateReport()   (line number: 546)
(bitmap is loaded with the invocation of decodeResource ())
which is called by  de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.download.DownloadService.java  onDestroy()

I am curious about the latter cases. Why these image loading operations are in main thread? 

Do you think perform image loading in the main thread will affect AntennaPod's performance? If so, perhaps moving the images loading to a work thread can help make app more smooth in user interaction.
Looking forward to your response.

Thanks.

title: Inefficient API is used
body:
Dear developers,

I found an inefficient API, setImageResource(), is used in AntennaPod.

For setImageResource(), Google says this:
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/widget/ImageView.html
" This does Bitmap reading and decoding on the UI thread, which can cause a latency hiccup. If that's a concern, consider using setImageDrawable(android.graphics.drawable.Drawable) or setImageBitmap(android.graphics.Bitmap) and BitmapFactory instead. "

I noticed that in the following code, setImageResource() is used:
de.danoeh.antennapod.core.util.playback.PlaybackController.java  (lineNumber: 484 )
 https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/util/playback/PlaybackController.java

Do you think the use of setImageResource() will affect AntennaPod's performance? If so, maybe we should move Bitmap reading and decoding to a background thread.

Thanks.

title: Handle slow/unresponsive podcast feeds

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
This is a feature request. For podcast feeds that are slow or temporarily unresponsive, Antennapod currently freezes and becomes unresponsive until the offending feed responds. Even killing Antennapod via Android's task switcher doesn't always clear the issue since it seems Antennapod tries to resume the last download it was performing before it was killed.

Ideally, it would be nice to have some sort of twiddler graphic to show Antennapod is still running, and hasn't gotten stuck due to some low memory issue, as well as some sort of cancel button for the current operation so if a podcast feed is down, you can cancel it and allow Antennapod to skip to the next feed. The app does currently show a progress bar and cancel button when the download or stream begins, but the issue here is happening before the download begins. The initial connection is timing out and Antennapod doesn't appear to check for this and hangs indefinitely.

I track a couple dozen podcasts, and this is making it very frustrating to use Antennapod because if even one feed is down, it means I can't use Antennapod. If I accidentally click on an item for a feed that's down, now Antennapod freezes for 10 minutes until I kill it.

An easy way to reproduce this problem is to setup a wireless router not connected to the Internet, connect to it's wifi, and then attempt to use Antennapod to stream or download a item on one of your existing feeds. The app will freeze and hang indefinitely and not report any status, forcing you to kill it.

**App version:** 1.6.2.3 (from Google Play)

**Android version**: 5.1.1 (CyanogenMod 12.1)

**Device model**: HTC One M7

title: Skip and seek with a single set of forward/backward hardware buttons
body:
I'm currently on version 1.6.2.3

I'd like to have an easy way to change episodes in the car without picking up my phone. I can enable the 'Forward button skips' preference, but it doesn't let you go backwards in the queue and it removes the ability to fast-forward (which is a nice feature since my car does not have separate fast-forward/rewind buttons).

My proposal is to support both fast-forward/rewind and skip to next/previous at the same time by assigning one action to a single tap, and the other to a double tap. e.g., If the user presses 'forward' once, then it fast-forwards. If they press it twice quickly, it skips to the next track.

I've implemented this locally to test the idea, and it works well for my use case so I'm interested in what other people think. The double tap works by waiting a small amount of time after a forward/backward request to see if another request comes in. If it does, it skips to the next/previous episode. If it doesn't, it performs the user's original request (reset to 0, ff/rw, etc.)

title: Feature Request: Save to Music folder
body:
**Use Case**: I listen to mostly music podcasts of DJ sets and sometimes want to listen to an episode many times. I would like to be able to save the podcast to my music folder. This is similar to the "Favorite" feature in function, but I would prefer to have the files I want to keep long term in the same location as all my other music. It also seems safer and more permanent to me - sometimes I'll find an abandoned podcast and want to save some of the episodes, but I'm not sure if I remove the podcast (since it never updates and doesn't need to be checked anymore) if I will lose the starred episodes when the podcast subscription is deleted. I think the separation makes sense - podcast client is for listening to new episodes, most of which I don't want to save. Music app and folder are for music I will keep long-term.

**Implementation**

1. One possibility I see would be to add the function to the 'Share' functionality. An option of "Save this episode to Music folder" would be added. Selecting this would copy the episode file to the Music folder. Arguably it doesn't fit the word 'Share" very well but since other app share buttons often go to services like Instapaper that provide personal archiving it seems like it wouldn't be too confusing or unobvious.

2. A second possibility would be to make this the optional behavior of the 'Favorite' function - clicking the star causes the file to copied to the Music folder. However, then the question is raised of what to do when the episode is unstarred, and whether the copy of the file in the Music folder should stay there or not.

**Issues**: I'm not an Android developer, so I don't know if the Music folder is a universal concept among all Android versions and flavors. It might require a setting to select the appropriate folder.

title: Feature to NOT add new episodes to play queue
body:
**App version:** 1.6.2.3 (from Google Play)

**Android version**: 4.1.2

**Device model**: Samsung Galaxy Ace 2 GT-I8160 (UK)

**Expected behaviour**: When a new episode is published, AntennaPod checks a configuration element to see whether it should be added to the play "Queue". Only add to the play queue if this option is enabled, otherwise perform other configured actions, e.g. download but do not add to play queue.

**Current behaviour**: All new (downloaded?) episodes are added to the play queue.

**Justification for feature request**: I have a wide range of podcasts that are configured to automatically download new episodes as they are published. When I decide to listen to podcasts, I want to chose the episodes that I want to listen to which may not necessarily be all the podcasts downloaded, e.g. I may want to listen to some comedy on my walk to the station in the morning but a drama on the train journey home in the evening. I want to define the play list for my listening manually.

**Proposed implementation**: I suggest a global Boolean configuration element, "Automatically add to play queue". This could be asserted by default to retain current behaviour, i.e. not change default behaviour of application. It may be advantageous to add a per-subscription option to override the global setting but I think the global setting is required. (My preferred workflow is to have no podcasts added to the play queue by default.) This setting may best be placed in the "QUEUE" section of the settings menu. (The settings menu is rather long so it may prove advantageous to add a sub-menu for queue management but that is not the subject of the feature request.)

Sometimes I'd like to choose a podcast episode based on how long it will take. I also use *speed* setting to speed up the playback.

It would be nice to show adjusted time after applying the speed. In other words, show the "[wallclock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall-clock_time)" time for the total episode length and/or for the remaining time left.

For instance, if the speed is set to `2.00×`, a 10-minute episode could show 5 minutes of total playback time. If the playback is at the 2-minute mark, then it could show the remaining playback time of 4 minutes (8 "virtual" minutes remaining).

Where to show this information? At the playback controls, it can be below the speed number, or right above the seek bar. This time can also be shown at the queue or at the episode list, but it can get very confusing, so I'm not sure if it is a good idea.

title: Loudness normalization (compressor/limiter)

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

labels.name: Needs: Decision
labels.description: Proposal and most arguments are clear, but needs a verdict.

body:
Some podcasts have wildly varying audio levels. It can be quite unpleasant to listen to them via headphones -- either you don't understand what's being said, or your ears start to hurt. This is also a health risk.

In technical terms, this is an issue of missing normalization during postproduction of the podcasts, or postproduction for a different target: Attentive listeners with a Hifi rack and speakers can appreciate voices talking softly and shouting alternately, while people with headphones, sitting on a train, jogging, or listening on car audio while driving can not. 

A basic audio effect can go a long way to fix this: We need a compressor, to push up the soft parts, and a limiter, to keep the loud parts within bounds.

There are some quite sophisticated solutions for this, e.g. auphonic. A good introduction in their blog: https://auphonic.com/blog/2011/07/25/loudness-normalization-and-compression-podcasts-and-speech-audio/

For Android, this opensource app seems to offer a normalization feature:
http://vipersaudio.com/blog/

I have also found this free compressor which focuses on PD apps:
http://cdm.link/2013/12/free-open-source-compressor-built-pd-perfect-mobile/

and this one, which is only "free as in beer" for use in apps:
http://superpowered.com/compressor-limiter-clipper#compressor

title: Feature request: accounts
body:
Currently I am subscribed to a bunch of podcasts for myself, but also a bunch of educational ones for my young kids. AntennaPod though gives me no easy to distinguish which should be played, short of only playing podcasts from one source.

Similarly, when I'm sitting on the sofa at home, often I'd like to watch some of my video podcasts, however, when I'm driving, I'd prefer to not be distracted by video based content. Similarly again, when I'm working, I'd really rather only have my music based podcasts playing. In short, often I would like to be able to play podcasts from one group of sources, rather than all of them or just one.

In contrast, Netflix let's me create a separate "account" which is essentially just a name, an image and a separate dataset for what's been watched etc. On opening the Netflix app, it just asks who's watching (if there's more than one account) and adjusts what is displayed accordingly.

My request is to set up a similar function on AntennaPod. The ability to create accounts would be done from the settings with an "Add an account" button, which would then let users enter a name and choose an image (with a random one assigned to begin with).

I have art/design skills (I'm the lead artist on The Secret Chronicles gpl game here on GitHub) so I'd be happy to help with creating a new set of profile image designs if needed.

Accounts would each have their own list of subscribed podcasts, settings and records of what has been listened to/watched. Each account could also be marked as an administrator or not, which would allow changing settings and adding/removing podcasts.

The advantage of an"accounts" based ui rather than something like subfolders, is the simplicity of being able to choose a source by simply tapping on a large, easy to hit button on startup, without slide out windows and scrolling etc. My kids can easily open Netflix, choose their account and hit play in a way they couldn't easily open AntennaPod and play a specific podcast right now. Similarly, if I'm trying to get a specific set of podcasts playing in a couple of seconds while waiting in my car at the lights, I could open AntennaPod, choose an account and hit play, where I'd be very lucky to open AntennaPod, pull out the slider window, scroll to a folder of podcasts only 1em high, tap that and then hit play... before the lights turned green.

Anyway, thanks for considering this. AntennaPod is already an amazing podcast client. For me, this would likely evolve it past that, to my family's primary media source. <3

title: OPML Import is not working from SD card
body:
---

It is impossible to import subscriptions from OPML file from SD card.
The following error message is displayed:
"Access to external storage is required to read the OPML file." with two buttons "Cancel" and "OK".
If you press "Cancel", the message disappears.
If you click "OK", it disappears for a short time and promptly appears again.

Should permissions be added for external storage access?

---

**App version:** 1.6.1.0, 1.6.1.2, 1.5.2.0

**Android version**: 2.3.4

**Device model**: LG P690

**Environment**: Rooted device, No Google Play Services installed

**Expected behaviour**: List of subscriptions from OPML file is displayed

**Current behaviour**: Error is displayed

**First occured**: Version 1.6.1.0

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Copy OPML file to any place on SD card
2. Open Add Podcast - OPML Import - From local filesystem - Choose the file - Press OK

title: OPML Import is not working
body:
---

When trying to import subscriptions from OPML file, nothing happens.
Rotating progress bar appears for a short amount of time and no subscriptions are added.
The functionality works well on 1.5.2.0 version with all else constant: same file, same location, same Wi-Fi connection.

---

**App version:** 1.6.1.0 and 1.6.1.2

**Android version**: 2.3.4

**Device model**: LG P690

**Environment**: Rooted device, No Google Play Services installed

**Expected behaviour**: All the chosen subscription are added to the podcast list

**Current behaviour**: None of the chosen subscription are added to the podcast list

**First occured**: Version 1.6.1.0

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Copy OPML file to File system root
2. Open Add Podcast - OPML Import - From local filesystem - Choose file - Press OK

title: Warn users when adding MP4/OGG feed
body:
[following https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/2101#issuecomment-244724762]

Quite often a reported 'bug' concerns an MP4 or OGG feed, while these formats are not well-supported by Android natively. To prevent a portion of these errors, it might be good to warn users when they try to add an OGG or MP4 feed.

When adding a feed by tapping on "Subscribe", it could check the filetype of the latest episode, and display a warning dialog with the text "You have subscribed to an OGG or MP4 feed. Android's support for these filetypes is sub-optimal. We suggest subscribing to an MP3 feed, if available." The dialog should also contain a don't-show-this-again-checkbox, I guess.

title: Edit feed URLs

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

labels.name: Good first issue
labels.description: Can be addressed without deep knowledge of the AntennaPod code. But exploring the code may be needed

body:
**App version:** 1.6.1.2 (from Google Play

**Android version**: 7 (Android N)

**Device model**: Nexus 5x

**Expected behaviour**: Being able to edit the feed URL of an existing subscription

**Current behaviour**: Currently it is only possible to copy the feed URL to the clipboard.

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Subscribe to a feed
2. Go to the feed
3. Tap on the (i)  (information) - there are details like URL - but no way for editing it
## Workaround

Delete existing subscription and re-subscribe.

Big disadvantage: all downloaded files are deleted and all the status flags are lost (e.g. which episodes were already downloaded and played).
## Possible Implementation

(i.e. the how): Just make the URL label editable in the subscription information dialog (which is reachable via the (i) icon, from the subscription tab).

This dialog already contains some editable fields like password/username or auto-delete-episodes.

Alternative: add an edit button right beside the existing copy-button.
## Motivation

From time to time some of my subscriptions has feed URL issues, e.g. the author changed the URL and screwed up setting up the redirection. In those cases I would like to just copy and paste the new URL into a feed configuration dialog to update just the URL.

BTW, from a UI design perspective, I find the (i) (information icon) isn't very intuitive. Before accidentally hitting it I searched multiple times in the preferences menu of that tab for a settings item. IMHO it would also be an improvement to add a menu entry to the settings menu (which already has the entries 'refresh menu', 'Flattr this', ..., 'Remove Podcast').

title: Auto-download loop on download error
body:
---

A radio show I listen updates the podcast rss before the airing adding an item with info about the upcoming episode but, obviously, without an url of the show.

the link, enclosure, guid tags looks like this:

```
<item>
...
  <link/>
  <enclosure length="10000" type="audio/mpeg" url=""/>
  <guid/>
</item>
```

after the show airs they update the podcast rss and the tags became like this:

```
<item>
...
  <link>http://audio.radio24.ilsole24ore.com/radio24_audio/2016/160917-conti-belva-s.mp3</link>
  <enclosure length="10000" type="audio/mpeg" url="http://audio.radio24.ilsole24ore.com/radio24_audio/2016/160917-conti-belva-s.mp3"/>
  <guid>http://audio.radio24.ilsole24ore.com/radio24_audio/2016/160917-conti-belva-s.mp3</guid>
</item>
```

I have auto-donwload active and when antennapod updates this podcast it tries to download a file that doesn'e exist and it loop. I have to manually disable autodownoad for that episode in order to stop from keeping popping-up error messages.

The podcast is this: http://www.radio24.ilsole24ore.com/podcast/conti-belva.xml
the show airs saturdays at 10am gmt+2 and the rss is updated usually friday evening without url. It then gets updated again when the show finishes at about 1pm gmt+2.

Here is the rss before and after: [gist](https://gist.github.com/nixxo/84cbcd12a3bc8abe1a12acb5eecf7ab6)

Hope you can fix it.

Cheers, nixxo

---

**App version:** 1.6.1.2 (from Google Play)

**Android version**: 4.4.4 [Paranoid android custom rom for sm-g350]

**Devide model**: sm-g350

**Expected behaviour**: Don't loop after the first error

**Current behaviour**: The apps keeps trying downloading and keeps displaying errors

title: HTML not rendered

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
With RSS the feed description tag only allows plain text, but the equivalent in Atom is [subtitle](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4287#section-4.2.12) and that does allow HTML.

In AntennaPod it gets [parsed](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/syndication/namespace/atom/NSAtom.java#L188) correctly, but when being viewed on either [FeedInfo](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/activity/FeedInfoActivity.java#L156) or [OnlineFeedView](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/activity/OnlineFeedViewActivity.java#L415) activities it is just displayed in a textview.

The best solution would be to render it in both places, I tried to do that but I don't understand the system in AntennaPod for displaying shownotes. If I could have, I would have done another pull request. The easier but more disappointing thing to do would be to trim the HTML like you do in the OnlineFeedViewActivity for shownotes.

title: Intermittent crashes near the start / end of episodes, during MediaSessionCompat.setMetadata()
body:
---

**Workaround**  (Sep 29 2016):
If your device is entry level or has little memory, try disabling lockscreen background in the settings. Disabling lockscreen background probably would alleviate most of the problems.

---

**Problem Summary**:
- When playing to near the end of episodes (or about to start the next one), Antennapod on my phone crashes intermittently but often enough (ballpark about 10% of time). 
- logcat indicated indicated OutOfMemory error (need to allocate 7.5Mb),  but I believed the device still enough of memory at that point (device had at least 30Mb free memory, though I understand it does not necessarily mean they are available to antennapod).
- The problem probably occurred around switching cover art `OutOfMemoryError` stacktrace shows it is triggered by `Bitmap.nativeCopy()` < ... ... < `MediaSessionCompat.setMetadata()` < `antennapod...PlaybackService$$Lambda$2.run()`

title: FR: Support filtering in Episodes screen all tab
body:
Use case: 
- I'd like to manually download some (older) podcast episodes, with no specific podcast in mind.
- So I go to Episodes screen > All tab, I found the episodes across all podcasts
- Pain point: the list is interspersed with all the downloaded episodes (grayed out), making it harder to browse for episodes. 

Note: this request sounds similar to #2118, but #2118 addresses the issue on podcast screen, while this feature request is for Episodes screen (across all podcasts)

---

Proposal:
- Add a filtering button. From user's perspective, it works the same way as the "3 dashes" filter button, allowing users to filter (and show) only not downloaded episodes.
- the UI will indicate the list is filtered: maybe adding circle-i icon to the tab title (the circle-i icon is from podcast screen). 
- Other options from podcast screen (played, not queued, etc.) can carry over for consistency sake. They may not make much sense in episodes screen, but might still fulfill some other use cases.

Thoughts?

title: filtering episodes
body:
Hi! I love antennapod and am very grateful for the open source app! I have just recently started using it (version 1.6.1.2 on Android 5.1.1) and here are two issues I can't figure out:
1. Basically, sometimes I need to filter episodes oldest to newest first - for listening to history podcasts for example. By accessing the "3 sprockets" settings button, episodes in a subscribed podcast can easily be filtered  in any possible way but when I return to the podcast page that certain filter gets lost. title: Playback event log

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Hello,

it would be great if application logged playback events of episodes somewhere (next to the episode/globally or both). The entries could be like:
- Episode X: started playing at position [mm:ss]  on [datetime 1] by [UI/headphones/bluetooth]
- Episode X: paused playing at [mm:ss] on [datetime 2] by [UI/headphones/bluetooth/sleep timer]
- Episode X: resumed playing at [mm:ss] on [datetime 3] by [UI/headphones/bluetooth]
  ....

Clicking (or long clicking maybe to avoid misclicks) on the entry would start playback at the specified position.

Not sure if this log should include rewinds/fast forwards in order to avoid cluttering the log. Probably not worth it in the first incarnation of the feature. Other improvements could include commenting on the entries later or e.g. capturing GPS location of the event.

Why would it be VERY useful for me? Well, sometimes I resume playback (without looking at the position first) and get distracted by something (but don't stop playback). Or better yet, I simply fall asleep sometimes even having no idea that I fell asleep :). So next time I would rather go back to the position where I started and figure out what I missed from there rather than try to figure out the same thing from the position I finally stopped the playback at (which is typically the end of the episode or another episode anyway, so this method is kind of useless :-) )

Think about it, this could also serve as a poorman's bookmarking in some sense ( https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/1946 ). You could "artificially" pause/resume playback (even better, do it via headphones) to get the log entry when you want to "bookmark". If you do not do this frequently, at least for me it is much easier to remember the datetime (that is a global "parameter" which you can approximate quite efficiently) rather than playback position which I have no idea about.

Thank you for considering. This would be a KILLER feature for me. Being a java programmer I was thinking about implementing this myself but I have zero Android experience and not much free time at the moment. So it would take quite a long for me.

Thank you making a great open source podcast app!

title: Feature Request: Support for Chapter-Images
body:
### What is a chapter image?

Chapter-Images are basically the same like a Chapter-Mark but have an image attached which could/should be displayed on the device when the related chapter is reached during playing the podcast. 
### Only few podcasts make use of chapters/images. Why should it get implemented?

In general only a few Podcatchers support Chapter-Marks and even less support Chapters-Images. An argument often stated is that not many Podcasts make use of these features but in my eyes this is a chicken-egg-question. I might be wrong but I think most of the time the services should offer a technology first so that users can make use of it.
### Do chapter-images make sense for an audio-only podcast?!

It's right, that he user would have to look at the smartphone/screen to see the image which makes no sense at first since we're talking about audio-only podcasts. But in fact, it's a wonderful feature.

For example here we've a German Podcast where Photographers talk intensively about 5 pictures over the course of a podcast episode (which goes ~2h). It's not mainly about the photo itself but more about the circumstances and situation where the photographer took the picture - still, it's just nice to see the photo they're talking about. Therefore, while listening, some times you can hear a "camera trigger"-sound which is placed at the position in the podcast where a picture got visible on your device. You don't have to, but now you can have a short look at the screen to see exactly what they're talking about (below you can find a link to this podcast).

http://bildsprache-podcast.de/bsp013-professor-rolf-nobel

I think this is a perfect sweet-spot between audio and video. The only alternative for showing a picture would be to 
- provide a video podcast (which would create a huge overhead for just showing off 5 pictures)
- force the listener to go to a website to look at the picture
- not to do a podcast like this - which would be a shame, because the podcast is awesome. :)

My personal project is a Game Development Podcast - sometimes the topics may be complicated. We'll try to describe them as well as possible with our voices but I'll include pictures when it might help for a better understanding.
### How have others implemented chapter-images?

The pictures would need to be visible within the chapter-mark-list. Here you can see an example of the Podlove WebPlayer on my website (https://gamedevpodcast.de/00/) and how iTunes does it:

https://media.gamedevpodcast.de/tutorial_chapterimages_01.png

You can see the image directly in the list (which in this case is a cat as an example-image). 
Imagine how useful this could be to find the chapter you're looking for - if you know they talked about "PacMan" or "C++" and the image in this list shows this as a graphic/logo, you don't even have to read through all chapter-marks.

**Important**: As soon as the chapter with the image is reached, a bigger version is displayed. In case of the Standard iOS Podcast App it looks like below: 

https://media.gamedevpodcast.de/tutorial_chapterimages_02.png

Here you can find a list of other programs which support chapter images at least in M4A:

http://gamedevpodcast.de/tipps/#podcatcher

By the way: It's super interesting that not only M4A but also MP3 supports chapters as well as chapter-images. I'm sorry for my long explanation but thank you soo much for taking the time!

Thanks for reading this long text and have a nice day!
Simon

title: Large MediaStyle notification (with large album on left) is not triggered

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Using Android 6.0 here.

I noticed that the MediaStyle notification is not actually triggered. This has two effects on the user experience:
1. The large album art in notifications, [which looks like this](http://i.stack.imgur.com/a7XDm.png), is not triggered.
2. The podcast's album art doesn't become my wallpaper when I'm listening to a podcast.

I found the reason that this was not triggering: MediaStyle notification only supports up to 3 actions in standard-size view aka `contentView` (and up to 5 in `bigContentView`). (See [MediaStyle documentation](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/support/v7/app/NotificationCompat.MediaStyle.html).) The app is currently attempting to display 4 actions in `contentView`: rewind, pause, fast-forward, and skip.

I verified, by testing, that reducing the number of actions to 3 does indeed trigger both large album art and album art as wallpaper.

Should we change the behavior of the app so that MediaStyle is triggered properly? If so, we should reduce the number of action buttons. Which action buttons should we remove?

title: hide episode button - 'one click hide'
body:
### Proposal

It would be neat to have a _hide episode_ button on **each** episode entry in the episode list of a podcast to be able to hide an episode from the list **with just one click/tap**.
### Justification

Let's assume that there are many podcasts that have many episodes of which quite a few are not interesting to the listener (which is true for me). I don't think it's a good idea and it's also not efficient to keep these uninteresting episodes in the list ... adding up with time. That's why a button to hide an episode **with just one click** would be nice. If there's many episodes to hide, I don't want to have to long press for the context menu and then do another click/tap.

AFAIK currently one can only long press on an episode (for the context menu) to mark it as played or use the advanced menu (to perform actions on multiple episodes), but that still keeps it in the list. Also misusing the _play status_ to hide non interesting episodes would make things more confusing since interesting episodes would also get the _played_ status.
### Implementation

As it currently looks the download button uses the whole height of an episode entry. I think this space would suffice for two buttons:_download_ and _hide_ stacked.

Of course the proposed feature would require an additional status of an episode: _hidden_
But it shouldn't be too difficult to implement, since statuses like _played_, _downloaded_ already exist.

title: Can't download some episodes from specific podcast
body:
**App version:** 1.6.0.9 (from Google Play)

**Expected behaviour**: Download episode

**Current behaviour**: Download says "File Type Error"

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Add podcast "El Mundo del Spectrum" from http://feeds.feedburner.com/ElMundoDelSpectrumPodcast.
2. Download any of the first episodes (at least from first season, 1x01, for example). It will fail.
3. However, download of last episodes (4x*) work ok.

Hi,
I've tried many things to see why I can't download some episodes from this podcast before posting this issue to make it more constructive, but I'm not sure which url uses AntennaPod to download them, so I'm afraid I can't help too much. The only difference I could see between a working episode and the others are that the content of the problematic ones uses ISO-8859-1 charset, not UTF8, but shouldn't Android internally take care about the encoding?

To verify if the episodes were really available I've tried another closed sourced podcast client and it could download those episodes without problems, so maybe we can find a workaround.

I've read some of the issues around here and maybe the PR at https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/pull/1938 is related. Should I try the nightly apk?

Thanks for your help.

title: Indicate "Marked as Played" episodes in Completed Downloads list

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
I would like for episodes that are "Marked as Played" to be easily visible when looking at the Completed Downloads list. I think the best way of doing this is for the played episodes to be grayed out, just like they are when looking at the podcast feed list. I would appreciate the chance to work on this feature.

When choosing which episode to listen to, I primarily choose episodes to listen to from the Completed Downloads list. This allows me to access all the episodes I have currently downloaded, from various podcasts, all on one screen. I also use this screen to delete episodes I have already listened to. Being able to quickly see what is "Marked as Played" will allow me to avoid accidentally replaying episodes that I already listened and to quickly delete the ones I've already heard.

I recognize that there is probably a better way for me to do this using the queue and the auto delete function, but this is just how I've been doing it and I think this feature would be useful for people like me.

title: Atom image

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
With atom feeds AntennaPod currently loads the image from the logo element. However the atom RFC states [logo should be a 2:1](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4287#section-4.2.8) image and [icon a 1:1.](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4287#section-4.2.5)

I think the easiest thing to do would be try to load the image from icon first and then fall back to logo when in the atom NS. Somewhere in [this file](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/syndication/namespace/atom/NSAtom.java).

However it might be better to allow multiple images in a [feed](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/feed/Feed.java). Then the two images in [feeditemlist_header](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/app/src/main/res/layout/feeditemlist_header.xml)/[ItemlistFragment](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/fragment/ItemlistFragment.java) could be different and not just a blurry stretched version of the same image.

title: Possible causes of Hang-Bugs Found

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Dear AntennaPod Developers,
I am implementing a hang-bug detection tool and I am analyzing AntennaPod with it (master version downloaded yesterday). I tested the app with a Nexus 4 (Android 5.1) and Huawei P8 Lite (Android 4.4). I found that the main thread of Antennapod calls:

1) android.database.sqlite.SQLiteCursor.getCount and
2) android.app.SharedPreferencesImpl$EditorImpl.commit

frequently when subscribing and opening podcasts. In particular, the above APIs are called as consequence of the two following calls:

```
1) de.danoeh.antennapod.activity.MainActivity.saveLastNavFragment -> android.app.SharedPreferencesImpl$EditorImpl.commit

2) de.danoeh.antennapod.core.storage.DBReader.getQueueIDList -> android.database.sqlite.SQLiteCursor.getCount
```

In my experiments, the execution of those functions on the main thread may be the main cause of the eye-detectable delays (i.e., hang-bug) experienced with AntennaPod.

As the developers guide of Android suggests, moving work off the main thread leads to higher responsiveness of the app. It is actually possible to move those two operations off the main thread using background threads. Therefore, do you think that the smoothness of the app would improve by executing those functions off the main thread?

Thanks for any information,
I hope I can help improve AntennaPod.

title: Performance Issue of AsyncTask.execute

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Developers of AntennaPod,

Hi, I have found that `AsyncTask.execute` has been used in many places, like 3 times in `GpodnetAuthenticationActivity`, one time in `AudioplayerActivity`, etc.
However, this API slows down if multiple tasks are being executed on devices with system version higher than 3.0 because AsyncTasks started by this API are executed serially on a single background thread for systems newer than 3.0. (This is found in the [API guide](http://developer.android.com/intl/zh-cn/reference/android/os/AsyncTask.html#execute%28Params...%29))
It will help to improve the performance by changing `execute` to `executeOnExecutor` to enable real multi-thread execution.

Thanks a lot.

Actually when I first saw the number in the Nav Drawer implemented (in the build for the ChromeCast test) I was like 'huh, I don't have that many subscriptions!?' In other words: I didn't read FR #1850 (by @Matth7878) properly and only now (sorry for being late) realised that to me the number should display the amount of subscriptions, rather than total amount of episodes.
- When the counter is set to '# of new episodes' both numbers (episodes & subscriptions) are exactly the same (and thus one of them is useless).
- Seems weird:
  - Queue: # of episodes in the queue
  - Episodes: # of (new) episodes
  - Subscriptions: # of subscriptions, no, wait, what, total # of episodes?
  - [Feed title]: # of [whatever set type of] episodes in that feed

Proposal:
- Episodes: total (sum) # of [whatever chosen in the settings: new/unplayed/combined] episodes [this is currently displayed after subscriptions]
- Subscriptions: # of subscriptions
- for both: don't display if counter setting=none (only number displayed = queue)

title: Threats of Crash on some Samsung devices

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Dear developers of AntennaPod,

I am a student majoring in Computer Science. We are trying to collect existing bug reports and fixes of bugs caused by specific devices to help detect and fix similar bugs of other active applications.

We have detected that in your app, method setSupportActionBar of android support library v7 is used in many activities. However, we have observed that invoking this method on some Samsung devices running 4.2 system will crash your app.

We have found discussions in in the bug tracking system of Android: [here](https://code.google.com/p/android/issues/detail?id=78377). as well as a stack overflow question: [appcompat-v7 v21.0.0 causing crash on Samsung devices with Android v4.2.2](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26657348/appcompat-v7-v21-0-0-causing-crash-on-samsung-devices-with-android-v4-2-2)

A suggested fix for it is to add `-keep class !android.support.v7.internal.view.menu.**,** {*;}` to the proguard rules. I have seen the opposite rule to keep all the classes in android.support.v7 in your proguard file.

Thank you vey much. Hope this information is useful for you.

title: Optimizations in PodDBAdapter.java
body:
In the ['PodDBAdapter.java'](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/b6ac166c4f88e139b294827bd5129ad28c040506/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/storage/PodDBAdapter.java), I see we have listed all the table field names as constants grouped together. It is very hard to understand the DB structure in this way. Wouldn't it be great if we group these so that by reading the code itself, I can imagine the database?

To implement this, we could create a static final class which we call `PodDBContracts.java`. In this file, corresponding to each table, we can create a static inner class which will have that table's field as constant strings. It would make the code more readable and maintainable. 

Please let me know if this is a welcome contribution right now. I would be happy to send a PR!

Harshita

I would propose a small set of changes to the 'apply actions' view. Currently, there are two distinct **filtering mechanisms**: one for the feed view, one for the 'apply actions'. They each have their own set of labels and function slightly differently. - let the filter applied in the episode view not affect the 'apply actions' screen - merge their strings (see table below): - add the 'paused' state filter in the 'apply actions' screen - let both filters have the same options order - remove 'all' and 'none' options from the 'apply actions' filter (these are already available via the 'select' button (next to the filter in the action bar) **And further**: - make it easier to see which episodes one has selected by a button that hides unselected items (so you don't have to scroll through the list to see which ones are selected) - button can be eg https://design.google.com/icons/#ic_visibility and [it's off state](https://design.google.com/icons/#ic_visibility) - once an episode is deselected it gets removed from the view (with a tiny delay so that the user can see the episode in fact is deselected) - for visual ease, align the 'select none/all' button in the action bar and the individual checkboxes - make the 'intermediate checkbox' deselect all rather than select all (more logical since the button has a minus sign)

| array (feed view) | seperate (apply actions) | value the same? | | --- | --- | --- | | hide_unplayed_episodes_label | unplayed_label | y | | hide_paused_episodes_label | n/a | n/a | | hide_played_episodes_label | played_label | y | | hide_queued_episodes_label | queued_label | y | | hide_not_queued_episodes_label | not_queued_label | y | | hide_downloaded_episodes_label | downloaded_label | y | | hide_not_downloaded_episodes_label | not_downloaded_label | y |

body:
**App version:** 1.5.2.0 (from Google Play), already had the issue in 1.4.2.2

**Expected behaviour**:
On the "Episodes" Screen I click on the refresh button to check whether new episodes of my podcasts are available. In the status bar Antenna Pod shows a shrinking number of how many feeds still must be updated. After all feeds are updated it shows the message "processing downloads" and after this is closed all new episodes are shown in the "Episodes" Screen.

**Current behaviour**:

- The message "processing downloads" persists. It seems to do something in the background all the time, because my battery is drained. The only chance to get rid of this is to kill Antenna Pod.

**First occured**: Version 1.4.2.2 / about 4-6 weeks ago/
I'm using Antenna Pod since beginning of year 2016. I already had the same problem in the end of January. I reinstalled Antenna Pod (which fixed the problem). About 4 weeks later, it appeared again. A week later I had no problem anymore, now it appears again.

**Steps to reproduce**:
It happens every time I update my feeds.
Before it happened the first time, this issue did not occure. I didn't change settings in-between.

title: Auto Delete deletes episode-in-progress after sd card unmount/remount

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
**App version:** 1.5.1.4 from play store. Haven't yet received an alpha/beta from joining the G+ groups

**Android version**: 6.0.1  (Stock AT&T)

**Devide model**: Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge

**Expected behaviour**: Episode in progress remains stored on the card and ideally continues to play from current play offset.

**Current behaviour**: Episode is deleted

**First occured**: Last Week, but that's when I first got this device and installed AP

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Configure AP with "Auto Delete" enabled
2. Configure AP to store podcasts on the SD card
3. Add at least one episode to the queue
4. Play an episode from the queue, leaving it paused somewhere in the middle
5. Unmount/remount the SD card
6. Hit Play on the episode - it will be deleted and the next queued one will play if "Continuous Playback" is enabled.

This issue is extremely annoying on the Galaxy S7 Edge. It currently has an issue where the SD card auto-unmounts quite often. There's debate as to whether it's a hardware or software issue. Since it always successfully re-mounts, I'm leaning toward some sort of power-saving software issue in Marshmallow. I also wonder if there's something in a recent Android API that AP can call to more completely "lock" the file and prevent the SD card from being auto-unmounted by the OS.
I'm guessing that Antennapod's open file handle gets invalidated so that resuming playback then fails (throws an exception?). It then proceeds as if it had completed playback of the episode and deletes it.

In this situation, where playback fails but the current position is nowhere near the end, I would not expect it to delete the episode. Ideally, AP could re-open the file in this situation and continue as if there had not been an error. I don't know if it will be easy (perhaps a specific exception type/error code) to tell that this is what happened.

For now, I've re-set AP to store casts on the internal storage to avoid the re-download or manual delete hassles. Not a solution for everyone.

- After restoring to not default location

original location:  android 4.4.4  /storage/sdcard1/Download/AntennaPod
restore location:  android 6.0.1  /storage/1234-ABCD/Download/AntennaPod (sdcard error)
working location:  android 6.0.1 /storage/1234-ABCD/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files
new location:       android 6.0.1 /storage/4321-DCBA/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files

/data/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/databases/Antennapod.db
/data/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/shared_prefs/de.danoeh.antennapod_preferences.xml

**>> Antennapod.db**
update "main"."feedimages" set file_url = replace (file_url, '/storage/sdcard1/Download/AntennaPod', '/storage/4321-DCBA/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files');
update "main"."feedmedia" set file_url = replace (file_url, '/storage/sdcard1/Download/AntennaPod', '/storage/4321-DCBA/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files');
update "main"."feeds" set file_url = replace (file_url, '/storage/sdcard1/Download/AntennaPod', '/storage/4321-DCBA/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files');

  <string name="prefDataFolder">/storage/4321-DCBA/Android/data/de.danoeh.antennapod/files</string>

- Show a visual difference between "live" items and only internally archived very old items. (according to last XML download)

Fancy / optional:
- auto algorithm (and setting - globally or per feed) for auto-limiting the feed list length to live items +N

title: flattr4j jarfile not available anymore (from wiki instructions on how to Set up the Android SDK)
body:
When setting my development environment following the [wiki instructions](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/wiki/Building-AntennaPod) I noticed that the link to `flattr4j` which points to http://www.shredzone.org/attachments/download/250/flattr4j-core-2.7.jar is now broken, as you get redirected to https://shredzone.org/index.html

There doesn't seem to be a place where to download the "compiled" jar file.

Also, the following is mentioned on the Github page of the project at https://github.com/shred/flattr4j :

> **Important Note**
> 
> Flattr is currently changing its API. Because of that, some of the flattr4j calls are failing or not delivering the expected results. It is unclear to me what a future API may look like, and to what extend flattr4j is going to support it. For the time being, **I recommend not to use flattr4j in new projects.**

So to create PR #1722 I didn't include this jarfile. The app runs fine, but as I have not been using Flattr since ~2013, I can't test the Flattr-specific bits.

Question: Is the Flattr integration from AntennaPod still working, or is it affected by the API changes mentioned above?

In any case, the wiki should probably be changed. The reason I didn't do it myself directly, is that I don't know what it should be changed to:
- either, if the code is broken, remove this .jar dependency (and thus also probably remove all Flattr code from the app?)
- or, if the code is still working, try to find another place where the jarfile can be downloaded from. (I suppose we don't want to ask new contributors to compile that jarfile, I for one have no clue what needs to be done for that, and am not interested in a `git clone` of that project's source code.

title: Prevent video controls from disappearing while using them

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
I suggest a change to the on-screen video controls. It would be nice if the controls do not disappear while using them. 

Currently, if I am playing a video podcast and hit the 30sec FF button (on the screen) several times, the controls will eventually disappear, no matter how frequently I am hitting the FF button. I can be rapidly hitting that button, and all of a sudden they on-screen controls disappear. Obviously they come right back after touching the screen again, but it may be nice to prevent them from going away.

It is good to have the on-screen controls disappear eventually, however, I suggest to keep the controls on-screen for a minimum number of seconds after touching a playback control button. Maybe 5 seconds. Then the controls should disappear after that.

Hopefully I am clear in my description.

title: Moving to new phone with newer version produced error in fetching feeds
body:
Hi!

I do not have apps from the play store set to automatically update, so when I switched to a new phone Antennapod was an older version (1.3.4.1). On the new phone the newest version of Antennapod was installed  (1.4.2.2). 

I backup the application data for Antennapod using Helium then restored it on the new phone. When I tried to fetch the feeds they all produced an **Unknown Error**.

I then tried upgrading the old phone to the newest version (1.4.2.2) of Antennapod and started Antennapod fresh and fetched feeds. This worked. I then backup Antennapod  on the old phone and restored on the new phone. I started Antennapod fresh and tried to fetch feeds. I got an **Unknown Error** for each feed it tried to fetch.

I then tried uninstalling Antennapod on the new phone. Then reinstalling Antennapod and  restoring the data with Helium.  I got an **Unknown Error** for each feed it tried to fetch.

I am not sure how to proceed other than I would need to start fresh and export  then import via OPML or via gpodder.net.

This means I will lose all my downloaded episodes and their status. Correct?

Any other ideas on moving Antennapod to a new phone?

Thanks again for all your hard work on Antennapod!
Frederick

title: Default episode cache size should be one of the options

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body: Currently, the default cache number is 20. But that's not one of the options (anymore). No real problem of course, but a bit weird.

title: FR: Export & import favorites
body:
Migrating from one phone to another, it's pretty damn easy to use OPML export & -import to move stuff over. Yet it would be great if also 'favourites' could be exported (given the fact that syncing with gpodder.net doesn't work properly in all cases), so that these episodes (and their feeds, as they can't be orphaned) could be imported to a new instance.

Currently, if gpodder.net is not enabled/functioning, ppl may loose their favourites (and not be able to re-add them, in they're old episodes which may no longer appear in updated feeds).

title: OPML Import: Select all/none toggle

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Currently, when importing an OPML file, 'deselect all' is hidden behind a menu button, and both 'select all' and 'deselect all' are still visible when it makes no sense to apply them.

Proposal: when none or a few (up to all but one) are selected) display 'select all', otherwise (in case everything is selected) display 'deselect all'.

This unclutters the UI, and (at least to me when migrating to a new phone) the only most logical thing to do is to select a few feeds manually, or everything via the button.

The rare case when 'deselect all' is wanted, is (I guess) when a person changes their mind:
A) first thought 'I want all' then thought 'I want just a few', or
B) first thinking 'I want feeds A-G' then thinking 'I want feeds Q-Z' (e.g. in case selecting many feeds manually and wanting to switch to another set.
In these cases users will likely figure out to press 'select all' and then 'deselect all'.

title: Can't see all audio controls

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
When using the phone on small screen in landscape, the audio controls can't be scrolled i.e. it's only possible to set the playback speed and left channel audio volume.

Version 1.5.0rc5 Android 4.4 Custom ROM

title: Episodes Skipping & Deleting
body: This has been happening sporadically over the last couple weeks and might coincide with an upgrade from Kit Kat to Lollipop. The issue is that I'll be listening to a podcast and suddenly I'm listening to the next episode in the queue. I thought that maybe I was inadvertently triggering this so I enabled "keep podcasts when skipping" but the episodes that skip disappear from my queue and need redownloaded to complete listening. Had this happen 3 times in 5 minutes on a drive tonight. I don't think this is happening while I have headphones in, just when connected to Bluetooth (hard to say though, I listen with Bluetooth 75% of the time).

title: Pause for interruptions
body:
I have enabled Pause for interruptions. This works fine for notification sounds. However, it doesn't work for other media sounds (e.g when Nike+ running is giving me an update on speed/pace)

App version: 1.4.2.2 (from Google Play)
Android version: 6.0.1 [stock]
Device model: Nexus 5x
Environment: Bluetooth headphones with Prestissimo

title: Duplicate items in podcast feed appear over time
body:
I've observed that sometimes multiple instances of items in podcast feeds appear over time. Following is an example:

![screenshot_2016-02-03-19-31-08](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5264535/12802761/1e7a2dac-cab3-11e5-9348-b4d3e70925c6.png)

The [podcast feed](http://cms.marketplace.org/podcasts/collections/153961/itunes) itself only defines one instance of each item. Initially when the podcast was added only one instance of each item was observed. Some time later after listening to all item, however, I went back and saw that there were multiple entires for each item. Some items have no duplicates, some appear 3x and some 4x times.

This is observed on AntennaPod 1.4.2.2 running on Android 4.4.2 from Cyanogenmod.

title: Breaks when updating android versions
body:
This has happened to me recently when upgrading my galaxy s4 (i9505) from stock 4.3 to cyangen 12, then more recently to cyangen 13.

Basically after the update antennapod loads and says 'external storage not mounted' I can't do anything in antennapod.

I managed to fix it both times by flushing the app data, which meant I had to manually subscribe again to every pod cast and download them all again.

From what I've seen online it seems to be where the previous path to the data (which I keep on an external sd card so my internal card doesn't get bloated) is invalid. 

Would it be possible to add an option when the expected storage path isn't found to redefine it?

title: AntennaPod won't write to external sd card
body:
I have an Xperia M4 Aqua running Android 5.0 and AntennaPod 1.4.2.2. I chose sdcard1 as the data folder (full path: /storage/sdcard1/Android/data/de/danoeh.antennapod/files). I then tried to download a podcast episode, but the message "Failed to access external storage" pops up.

Also, if the path stated above is selected, OPML Import doesn't work, either. Internal storage must be selected for it to import subscriptions successfully.

title: AntennaPod fails to recognize downloaded podcasts after unmounting and remounting
body:
I recently attempted to move my podcasts manually to my SD Card due to space concerns. However, as other posters- have mentioned, AntennaPod does not recognize files that are moved manually. It is for this reason that I deleted my stored podcast data and reinstalled AntennaPod. However, now with the podcast directory on the external storage, every time I mount and unmount the SD card, AntennaPod no longer recognizes the downloaded podcasts (doesn't allow playback and starts to redownload the previously downloaded podcasts) -- similar to how it doesn't recognize podcasts that are placed in the media directory manually. 

Any assistance relating to this matter would be very much appreciated. 

Thank you!

EDIT: Additional Information

Android version: 5.0.2 (CyanogenMod 12-20150308 Nightly Build)

Device model: Samsung Galaxy Note 3 (SM-N9005)

Expected behavior: Expected AntennaPod to playback downloaded podcasts after unmounting and remounting SD card,  

Current behaviour: The play icon appears next to the downloaded podcasts, but once I choose to play the files, AntennaPod begins to redownload them

AntennaPod Version 1.4.2.2

Steps to reproduce:
1. Choose external storage for data folder.
2. Download any particular podcast episode.
3. Close AntennaPod, unmount the SD Card and remount. 
4. Open AntennaPod and attempt to play the previously downloaded podcast -- a recommencement of the download should occur.

title: Leaving cursor in sleep timer crashes v1.5.0.rc3
body:
[v1.5.0rc3_release](https://www.dropbox.com/sh/4h2kfa2d2jesnu8/AAD46nRoaLoo_CRU03jkG1OOa/AntennaPod_1.5.0rc3_release.apk?dl=0) reliably crashes, whenever I leave the cursor in the sleep timer field for a few minutes and then wake the phone (Galaxy S4 mini / i9195) up again.

I tested playback speeds 1 and 1.4, .oga and .mp3 files, switching the screen off via the power button and waiting for auto-screen-off and leaving a number in the sleep timer field vs. deleting the number (in which case it says "Ente" BTW).

title: Custom media location
body: Currently, the only customization option for download location is the ability to choose the storage device AntennaPod uses. There should be some way, perhaps a field in the settings menu, to set a custom directory as the location for completed podcasts, i.e. sdcard1/Podcast.

title: Resuming incomplete downloads sometimes results in duplicated content

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Sometimes when downloading a file the download cannot complete for one reason or another. When the download is re-attempted / resumed, it eventually can succeed. The interesting bit is that when the file is finally played, it sometimes has a section of audio repeated around where the download failed and was restarted. That is, the audio plays, then at some point the last few seconds repeat. However, the issue is not the playback, as once the file is downloaded the repeating bit can always be reproduced.

It is also possible that when the download is continued from being interrupted the resulting audio file may contain a section which is invalid and sounds like static when played for a brief moment around the section where the re-download occurred.

This can be observed on AntennaPod 1.4.2.2 from F-Droid.
