title: Old episodes re-downloaded
body: With the latest update (1.5.0.2) I'm getting a regression of and old issue I posted a while back (on phone so couldn't find it, will check when I'm on my computer again). Episodes that I've already listened to, in October and November, are downloaded and added to my queue with automatic download enabled.

title: When subscribing via iTunes search I get on gpodder.net podcast named "Unnamed Podcast"
body:
I have searched on iTunes for the podcast "Blue Ocean World". I subscribed to it (and I don't need to emphasize, right?, that I am very grateful that AntennaPod allows me to search subscriptions on iTunes). When downloading the subscription correctly propagated to my gpodder.net account as well, and it has correct name and issues in the AntennaPod. However, when I look on the subscription on gpodder.net, I see it named as "Unnamed Podcast". That is not good.

It's true RSS stream turns out to be http://www.hellohoratio.com/podcast.xml (and if subscribe to it on gpodder.net via this URL then it gets name, issues, correctly).

Is there something wrong with propagating metadata obtained from iTunes?

title: RFE: Multiple playlists /queues
body:
I would love to be able to make multiple playlists. For example one for news and another one for documentaries. 

An example of usage would be the history podcasts by Dan Carlin. They're long and should be heard in the correct order. I would make a playlist of one period of history (as Dan does in his naming structure of podcasts). Then I could listen to topical podcasts of news and current affairs for a while, and when I have more time I can listen to another one is a series of history podcasts.

Maybe a solution could be an ability to add tags to podcasts, manually and automatically, and then create, sort and play queues based on tags?

Related topic: sorting the order of podcasts is not very 'discoverable'...

title: Skipping episode does not update player view

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body: On AntennaPod 1.5.0.2 when an episode is skipped from player view info for current episode is not updated : episode image, podcast name and episode name do not change and info from previous episode is still displayed.

title: OPML export saves in folder that gets removed on uninstall
body:
When you do an OPML export, it gets saved in the antennapod folder, which gets deleted if you uninstall it. This is rather unfortunate, as keeping the data even though you're uninstalling the app is rather the point of the OPML export.
Could this be changed so it either saves it in someplace which doesn't get deleted, or doesn't delete that specific file when uninstalling?
As a secondary concern, doing two exports results in only one file. Does it get overwritten? I suggest saving it with timestamps in the name or just numbering them.
Thirdly, maybe you should by default leave some settings and subscription data behind when uninstalling? You make it far too easy to lose all settings and subscriptions.

Sincerely,
A quite grumpy settingless and subscriptionless user

Nexus 5 | AP v.1.5.0.2 | Android 6.0.1

title: Introduce "Top queue item" setting for continuous playback

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

labels.name: Needs: Decision
labels.description: Proposal and most arguments are clear, but needs a verdict.

body:
> while I am at it I would like having the player start playing from the top of the queue when new episodes are added. Of course after the current episode is played.
> @cdysthe in https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/1414#issuecomment-159448272

Wholeheartedly agree. Currently, the 'add to top of the queue' option doesn't make much sense: Imagine a line (queue) to enter a concert, where VIPs may enter at the front of the line (add episodes to top of the queue). Then what's the point of having ppl added in front of the line (top of the queue) if you let ppl enter (episodes play) who are half-way in the line (just because they happen to be behind the person that last entered). The logic of a line (queue) I think is: first in line, first entrance (rather than first next person in line after the one that just entered).

Then why still add episodes to the top if playback starts somewhere in the middle? The aim (in my world) of 'add to top' is to make the queue have the most recent episodes first. However currently playback will always end up somewhere in the middle of the queue, and I won't always listen to the most recent episodes first.

Currently I always manually drag & drop the currently playing episode to the top, which is really cumbersome.

Curious to see @mfietz' & @TomHennen's viewpoints. If not standard behaviour, I'd advocate for a setting to enable this (new setting under 'Queue').

title: Continuous playback if initiated from podcast screen (+ reversed)

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
I sometimes like to listen to a bunch episodes from one show, just to catch up with the feed after holidays. Currently, this is possible by manually sorting the queue, but I find it quite a hassle to do so. Quite some other users seem to want to be able to play the episodes just from one feed, because they're listening to an audio play, lectures, or alike.

Therefore I'd like to propose:
- to make AP **play the next episode in the feed list when the currently playing episode is finished, when playback is initiated from the feed list** rather than from the queue
- to **introduce a new feed-setting to reverse the order in the feed screen** so that the newest episode of the feed would be shown at the bottom of the list (and new episodes would be added to the bottom). If enabled, I can then listen to that episode in sequential order by tapping on the highest listed (and thus the oldest) episode, after which AP will continue playback down the list (to more recent episodes).
## 

**Feed screen as dedicated queue, change of perspective (?)**
I have the feeling often we as (wannabe-)developers\* see the feed screen as a way to manage episodes of that particular feed, and a way to reach information and settings of that feed. Given the large amount of talk about multiple playlists and stuff, however, I believe many people could easily or already see/perceive the feed overview as a special playlst or dedicated queue for one show, and I think we should adapt our perspective accordingly. When doing so, the proposed makes more sense than current behaviour, regardless the use case. Rather than jumping from one queue to the other (dedicated to general) without any feedback to the user, AP sticks to the queue from which the user initiated playback.

 \* I consider myself to be one of the wannabe-developers

title: Unavailable episodes (no media file) in "New" list

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Here's a frequent offender: http://www.kqed.org/.pod/forum
They add new entries without media content, then add the content to the entry several hours (days?) later.

In AP, these new "episodes" show up with a "mark as played" check mark instead of download icon. There seems to be no way of adding these episodes to the queue (so I can remember to download them later, when they become available)
If marked as read/played, these don't reappear as new when actual content is added later (even if the updated feed now includes content)

A similar (but slightly different) offender: http://www.sciencefriday.com/feed/podcast/podcast-video/
Adds links to the media file, but the media file is not available (HTTP/404) for some days.

Possible solutions:
1) implement a "download queue" -- use standard download rules, but don't start the download until the media file is available. If media file unavailable, don't remove from download queue.
This is probably the best solution, though most effort to implement...
2) allow adding episodes without media to the queue -- let user download manually later
3) when media file becomes available, episode should be re-added to the "New" episode list

title: When connected to WiFi that doesn't provide internet connection, download files hang playback

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Antennapod should verify that the data downloaded is the media data.
If connected to a hotel or airport Wifi that require further login, the downloaded file is small, around 1-20 kb.  It is probably the network login screen, but antennapod assumes that it media file and trys to play it.  Which generally hangs the program and it is killed.

A connection with blocking, may also have similar problems, where the blocking message is received instead of the media data.

I suggest two corrective actions:
1. Verify that the internet connection is available, before attempting to download the episode.
2. Check that the received data is actually a valid media file after it is received. If not, don't let it be played.  

Workaround: Look for media files that are too small and delete them from the cache manually.

I also have problems where antennapod hangs when an audio podcast ends, followed by a video.
Again, checking the data, before attempting to play it should allow using the correct codec.  The check should be done on the next podcast in background while playing the first podcast or when it approaches the end.

Proposal: update interval is set to 24 hours

title: More smark options

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Usually podcasts last way longer than songs, 60 and 90 minutes are quite common. And many of them have 'garbage' (ads, uncut overlapping times from other contiguous chapters or programs), that you would like to skip especially at the end of the episode, all while considering current episode as fully played.

I guess that this is why a 'smart mark as played' optional time is offered; you can currently choose between No and 15/30/45/60 seconds.

I would like to request to expand this to allow to select for several minutes. For example, my typical podcast has usually around 5 minutes of overlapping content at the end I have to skip to go to next episode. I would bet that 5 minutes for something 60/90/120 minutes long is way more frequent than 60 seconds, the longest I can choose. Adding 5 and 10 minutes to the current available options would more or less make it for many people with minimal developer effort.

Alternatively, I would rather prefer to let me choose the amount in seconds I want, instead of being only offered a closed set of predefined values. This way developers would not need to guess which options to offer, simply let the user enter what they feel it fits him. That would be slightly more complicated to code, but not much; perhaps only some code to prevent absurdly high or negative values to be accepted would be in order for safety.

title: Understanding translation
body:
So I suspect the following files are related to translation of AP, but could someone confirm, correct and/or expand if needed?
- [AntennaPod/.tx/config](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/.tx/config) → The transifex project configuration. Indicates which translation files (eg trans.fr or trans.sv_SE) need to be placed in which folder in the codebase
- [AntennaPod/core/src/main/res/](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/tree/develop/core/src/main/res) → The folder in the codebase where all translation files are stored. Each language has its own folder, eg values-fr or values-sv-rSE, with in that folder a strings.xml file.
- [AntennaPod/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/util/LangUtils.java](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/core/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/core/util/LangUtils.java) → creates an array in the app with language codes and their written-out names.

And finally, another question:
If I'd change the Transifex configuration file and do a pull request to add another language that's been translated on Transifex (and let's say the PR gets accepted), would that mean that automatically with the next import from Transifex (by the main developers), the right folders in AntennaPod/core/src/main/res/ would be created?

title: Introducing a language threshold
body:
Following the discussion in #1369 and earlier thoughts, I would like to propose a translation threshold for including languages in the app. If a language has less than that threshold translated (the 'English' resource, not considering the description or changelog), then we shouldn't provide it in the app. This would create a cleaner interface in the app itself. But it also relates to the question of claiming which languages you support in Google play, maybe later on the website as well: if you have just 50% translated, than it wouldn't be fair to claim that language is supported. Though a bit arbitrarily, I would suggest a threshold of 75%. This would cut off the following languages: - Hebrew (Israel) 74% [he_IL] - Russian (Russia) 74% [ru_RU] - Polish (Poland) 68% [pl_PL] - Danish 68% [da] - Portuguese (Brazil) 62% [pt_BR] - Greek 59% [el]
NOTE: Greek is currently not imported from Transifex either - Hindi (India) 52% [hi_IN] - Italian 49% [it]
NOTE: Italian (Italy) // 85% // Nov 01, 04:03p.m. // [it_IT] _is_ available, so `it_IT` can be used for `it` - Romanian (Romania) 44% [ro_RO] - Azerbaijani 38% [az] - Spanish (Spain) 35% [es_ES]
NOTE: Spanish // 100% // Nov 03, 05:03p.m. // [es] _is_ available, so `es`can be used for `es_ES` - and other languages with less than 35% of the strings translated I put the languages that _will_ be available on the wiki: [Supported languages](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/wiki/Supported-languages) I would be willing to spend some time activating people to update the languages that are just below the threshold.

title: Norwegian (Bokmål) not imported from Transifex
body:
Comparing the list of [languages translated](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/wiki/Supported-languages) to [this Transifex import list](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/.tx/config) (if that indeed is what it is), it seems that Norwegian Bokmål (Norway) // 99% // Nov 01, 04:03p.m. // [nb_NO] is fully translated but not imported from Transifex.

`Bokmål ([ˈbuːkmɔːl], literally "book tongue") is an official written standard for the Norwegian language, alongside Nynorsk. Bokmål is the preferred written standard of Norwegian for 85% to 90%[2] of the population in Norway.` ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bokm%C3%A5l))

Given the above, I assume [nb_NO] strings could also be used to cover [no].

Unfortunately, the system doesn't rely on GitHub data and new feature 'requests' created on the platform don't lead to features created on FeatHub, and vice versa. However, the community (including me) can make sure cross-linking happens between feature requests on GitHub and FeatHub.

A list of the most-voted features can be [embedded](http://feathub.com/feathub/feathub/+1) in the AP website and/or the project page here on GitHub.

(I found this as I was originally searching something to implement [this voting-system](https://widget.uservoice.com/omnibox/ZvXzkjQWXCAPzzA85v84cg?mode=support&locale=en&forum_id=137101&contact_us=true&mixpanel_channel=site2_sidebar&embed_type=inline) in an easy way).

title: User survey
body:
To improve the website (https://github.com/AntennaPod/antennapod.github.io/issues/4), prepare for a 'Warm welcome' (#1329) and prepare for a new logo (#1281), it would be nice to start a user survey to gather some input from the users of AntennaPod.

This survey could cover the following **topics**:
- Feature usage frequency
- Most-liked currently implemented features (Ranking)
- Most-wished not-yet-implmemented features (Ranking + user input)
- Can we get in touch again for one follow-up survey? (e.g. for logo-vote)
- User-profile: country, age category, amount/situation of use, visual/hearing/other handicap that might limit usage
- Feedback/comments (Open text field)

For **data collection** we could rely on a Google form or a [Qualtrics](http://www.qualtrics.com/), [SurveyGizmo](https://www.surveygizmo.com/survey-software-features/question-types/) or [Opina](http://opinahq.com/) survey, or try to self-deploy a survey using [LimeSurvey](https://www.limesurvey.org/en/)

title: Starting Bluetooth playback on reconnect doesn't always work correctly

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
The best example is when your device is paired with a car stereo.  AntennaPod will start playback as soon as the device connects to the car.  However, the car stereo may not have the Bluetooth source selected. As a result AntennaPod podcasts will be playing through episodes, but the user will have no idea this is happening. As far as they're concerned they just started their car and are driving somewhere listening to the radio/cd/nothing.

One thought for how to resolve this so that it works properly for people with Bluetooth headsets is to have a setting that determines if AntennaPod will start playback on bluetooth reconnect.  It has also been suggested that AntennaPod should vibrate some when it starts playback due to a Bluetooth reconnect.

This behavior changed in AntennaPod 1.4 alpha, so I think we should try to resolve it before we release 1.4.

title: Android home screen widget requires first opening main app
body:
Phone: Motorola Moto X 2011
Android Version: 5.1
Kernel version: 3.4.42-g756aa87
AntennaPod version: 1.4.0.2

The home screen widget is a 1-high-by-4-wide widget that lists the podcast's title, includes a track progress time indicator in the form of "current hh:mm:ss / total hh:mm:ss" and a play/pause button.

If the AntennaPod app has not recently been opened, is not listed in the recent apps list, or was at some point exited by the Android OS to clear up RAM, the widget does not fully work. In this situation, you see the most recent track's title and the play button, but no progress/total time. Upon hitting the play button, I do see it's on/off-touch actions as the background highlights, but it does not start playing. 

At this point, I see two options:

Option 1: First open the app (using its main icon or clicking elsewhere on widget) and then hit the play button. Now it's registered, and so when you go back to the widget, you now see the current/total time and the widget's play button will function.

Option 2: First open the app (using its main icon or clicking elsewhere on widget), but then do **not** actually hit the play button. Go back to the widget. If you do this, the play button will now function, but the area of the widget which _should_ show the current/total time is still blank. Once this happens, I can't figure out how to get the current/total time to show on the app again. Play/pause it as much as you want, either from the widget or within the app, it looks like the current/total time will not return to the app until the app is cleared from memory (by Android or by you manually) and you execute the steps listed above in Option 1.

I know this is really corner case stuff. You have no obligation to address my issues, I'm just happy to provide you information.

title: Updated description
body:
As @TomHennen suggested in https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/1152#issuecomment-138323471, I've been working on re-writing the app description.

**Below is my proposal. If you feel like adapting it, it's easiest to go over to [this TitanPad](https://titanpad.com/9y3ic3NMWv).** Please do fill in your GitHub username if you make changes; it makes any discussion easier. Please also provide some explanation if you changed things in the chat facility there.

I'll only do a PR to change https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/develop/description/en.txt if some consensus has been reached on the change (hence the TitanPad).
# Proposed description

With AntennaPod you get instant access to millions of free and paid podcasts, from independent podcasters to large publishing houses such as the BBC, NPR and CNN. Add, import and export their feeds hassle-free using the iTunes podcast database, OPML files or simple RSS URLs. Save effort, battery power and mobile data usage with powerful automation controls for downloading episodes (specify times, intervals and WiFi networks) and deleting episodes (based your favourites and delay settings).

But most importantly: Download, stream or queue episodes and enjoy them the way you like with adjustable playback speeds, chapter support and a sleep timer. And show your podlove to the content creators with our Flattr integration.

Made by podcast-enthousiast, AntennaPod is free in all senses of the words: open source, no costs, no ads.

All features:
- Easily add and import feeds via the iTunes and gPodder.net directories, OPML files and RSS or Atom links
- Manage playback from anywhere: homescreen widget, system notification and earplug and bluetooth controls
- Enjoy listening your way with adjustable playback speed, chapter support (MP3, VorbisComment and Podlove) and an advanced sleep timer (shake to reset, lower volume and slow down playback)
- Take control over automated downloading: choose feeds, exclude mobile networks, select specific WiFi networks, require the phone to be charging and set times or intervals
- Manage storage by setting the amount of cached episodes, smart deletion (based on your favourites and play status) and selecting your preferred location
- Share episodes and feeds through advanced social media and email options, the gPodder.net services and via OPML export
- Support content creators with Flattr integration including automatic flattring
- Keep track of the best of the best by marking episodes as favourites
- Find back that one episode through the playback history or by searching (titles and shownotes)
- Access password-protected feeds and episodes
- Take advantage of paged feeds (www.podlove.org/paged-feeds)
- Back-up your subscriptions with the gPodder.net integration and OPML export

title: More extensive Cleanup settings

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
# Current (as per #1241)

![cleanup_settings](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5216560/10257690/df66355e-6926-11e5-9ff2-75c2ad425fc3.png)
# Enhencement

A bit more flexibility in these settings could be nice:

**Remove episodes:**
- After: [radio buttons]
  - completing playback [default]
  - pausing(/skipping) or completing playback
- With a delay of: [dropdown]
  - 0 days (immediately)
  - 1 day [default]
  - 3 days 
  - 5 days
  - 7 days
- But exclude: [checkboxes]
  - favourites [default: Y]
  - episodes in the queue [default: Y]

The advantage of adding 'remove after pausing' is that if you loose interest of an episode and tap 'next' halfway through, these episodes can be automatically deleted after a while and won't take up memory space indefinitely.

**What if you just pause and want to listen to an episode later again?**
Because many people just pause an episode with the intention to listen to it again later, this option should not be the default. In practice, this setting I imagine will almost always be applied in combination with a delay of a couple of days; when the episode has not been restarted after those days, there's probably a lack of interest (this would be my use case, with a setting of 5 days).

**inspiration**
Use-case of @charlesay in #1262.

title: Playback position regularly moves back to pre-last position after pause

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Often, but I can't tell in which cases exactly, the playback position of an item regularly moves back to pre-last position after pause. What I mean with that is:
- I play an item and pause it (playback time A). (some stuff happens in between) then play again and pause again (playback time B)
- when resuming the play again, the progress bar and currently playing position show correct data (playback time B) for half a second or so, but then changes to playback time A.

What I don't know:
- if it happens only when I pause it via the lock screen, or when playback gets paused when I unplug my earbuds, or when I manually pause it in the playing bar at the bottom or the system notification
- if it happens with certain 'some stuff happens in between' (i.e. play another item, refresh feeds, shutdown phone, check email, etc)
- if it also happens if I only paused once (playback time A being 0, basically) [I think it does sometimes, but I'm not sure]

This issue has been present for quite a while (throughout some different versions). Don't know why I only reported it now. I have not enabled prestissimo. The issue plays up I think for different feeds.

I found it rather cumbersome to note down every single pause and the consequence in daily use (playback gets paused rather often) and thus I didn't do it. Any feedback on if it's really necessary to do so (to provide more detailed info) or on other means of getting more detailed info is appreciated.

AP v. 1.3.4.1 on Android 4.2.2

PS. My quick-fix is to pay attention to the position when I hit play, so that I can manually scroll to that position again.

title: PROTOCOL_ERROR

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Recently I tried to listen to the System Mastery podcast. The feed's here:

http://feeds.feedburner.com/SystemmasteryPodcasts?format=xml

It's hosted on Wordpress. The feed loads fine but I get a PROTOCOL_ERROR in AntennaPod. I get the same error in Pocketcasts. The audio files download just fine with desktop clients, curl, etc. The System Mastery folks are at a loss as they didn't change anything, but were getting reports from their users things didn't work properly.

I went looking around and found this issue:

https://github.com/square/okhttp/issues/1897

so it's possible that there is some change in Android 5.x that in combination with a server change (HTTP 2 support on part of Wordpress?) triggers this problem.

I recently learned another podcast, Heavy Cardboard, also hosted on Wordpress, is experiencing very similar issues with Pocket Casts. According to them Pocket Casts is working on a fix but I figured I'd inform you too.

http://feeds.feedburner.com/HeavyCardboardPodcast?format=xml

title: Use built in APIs in Android 6.0 for variable speed playback
body: API 23 added the PlaybackParams class that allows for (among other things) setting playback pitch and speed. These params can be attached to a MediaPlayer object. Because of this, Prestissimo should be considered deprecated as of Android 6.0. Use the native API instead.

title: dial playback speed down to 1.0 during sleep timer

It could work by simply distributing the `Playback Speeds` steps along the `Sleep Timer`'s time axis with the 1st "downstep" happening immediately.

Example: Speeds 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 and 1.75 are set upBefore starting the timer, playback is at 1.5x. Setting the sleep timer to 20min, the first 10min play at 1.25 (immediate downstep) and the last 10 at 1.0. If 1.75x was used before and 30min are then timed, 10min each would play at 1.5, 1.25 and 1.0.

title: Freeing up space in the nav drawer
body:
As to not take over the main discussion in #836 about a special feeds-screen, I'll continue the discussion here about my proposal to move down the 'add podcast' entry in the navigation drawer to below the list of individual feeds, plus the proposal to unpin settings, both in order to free up space higher up in the menu. My reply to the comments by @Cathryne:

> Do I understand correctly, that these suggestions would make the "distance-to-option" dependent on the number of subscribed podcasts?

Yes

> If yes, why punish listeners with many subscriptions in this way?

Well, I guess that's one way to look at it ^^ Instead of focussing on a negative attitude of developers/the programme ('punishing the listeners'), I would like to look at the likelyhood of an option being used. I don't know about you, but personally, and I would think many users with me, tap on a feed in the drawer far more often than they tap on 'Add podcast'. If this is indeed is the case for most users, then to me it only makes sense to put the 'add podcast' entry below the feed list in the drawer. The less often a function gets used, the higher its' "distance-to-option" can be (and vice versa). Plus, the larger the list of 

> It's IMHO fine to have a few items pinned (configurable & rather at the top, than at the bottom, but hey!).

Sure, it's absolutely fine to have a few items pinned. But, again, following the reasoning above, the "distance-to-option" relative to how often a function is used, would make it only logical to not have the settings pinned. Indeed this is in line with (current) [Material Design guide](http://www.google.be/design/spec/patterns/navigation-drawer.html#navigation-drawer-content).
And pinning items at the top I feel really goes against all UI/UX conventions :P

> In order to clean up space the vertical space of each item & podcast title should be reduced. The necessity to shrink the covers in the drawer to about half their current size would IMHO be balanced out by aa separate subscription view with large cover images (not sure I'd use it, because I really like the drawer list).

title: Can't remove subscriptions with dead RSS feeds
body:
I synced with my gpodder.net account, which included several subscriptions that no longer have active RSS feeds.  It seems that since AntennaPod has never successfully downloaded the feed, it doesn't appear in the subscription list, so I can't remove the dead subscription.  I have unsubscribed via gpodder.net, but AntennaPod doesn't seem to be syncing the _removal_ of a subscription.  As a result, every time I refresh my podcasts, I get errors for four RSS feeds that I don't have listed in my subscriptions.
Also, is there a way to get to the download history / error log from inside the app?

body:
I'm using the F-Droid build of 1.3.1, but since updating to it, I don't seem to be able to set the interval (or time of day) to check for new episodes. Settings->Update Interval or Time of Day->Set Interval and then it doesn't matter what I choose it doesn't seem to take. I have Mobile Updates and Automatic Download turned off, but I'm on WiFi a lot.

I didn't see this listed already, but maybe I missed it or it's already being fixed or it's specific to the F-Droid build.

Thanks.

title: Battery: Persistent CPU wakelocks when inactive
body:
Hello,
Today I did not use my Phone and the battery went from 80% to 10% in a few hours.
A look in Wakelock Detector told me that my Phone was active all the time. AntennaPod (more exactly: com.aocate.media.ServiceBackedMediaPlayer) prevented the CPU from sleeping for 93% of the up time (since 1d and a few hours)!
During this period I was in flight mode, did not listen to any episode and nothing was paused, either. So AntennaPod should have been (almost) completely inactive.

After I forced AntennaPod to exit the battery stayed at 10% for 3 hours :)

I use CyanogenMod 12.1 and AntennaPod 1.3.1.

title: Audio-normalisation (& volume correction)

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Taking the feature request by @Threore in the issue on enhancements for AP v 1.3:

"I do a lot of my podcast listening while riding to university on a bicycle, which means wind and traffic often make it hard to hear the podcasts. The obvious solution is to turn the volume up, but **some podcasts are so much louder than others that going from one to the other becomes jarring. Some setting or automatic feature that normalises all the audio would be great**."

Same for me; sometimes I'll just pull out my headphones on the bike when I can't hear what they're talking about on a new episode from the queue (no, I don't have buttons on my earplugs to skip episode or adjust volume :) )

I would like to add the option to set audio levels to the softer, middle or louder podcasts (I know this boils down to an additional volume setting front-end, but back-end it would be determining the volume edit between finishing normalisation and saving the file). Reason: normalisation may not be enough to pump up the volume high enough to suit biking (although maybe I'm wrong here).

title: License
body:
With the growth of the project, the [current](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/b332942f161f598d2c3247bdd073765a8ad51662/LICENSE) license is probably no longer sufficient as it leaves much unclear and not explicit. For example, it asks for the copyright notice to be included, but doesn't say anything about whether forked code should disclose source code or not (relevant [comment](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/997#issuecomment-128245418))

It's probably a good idea for the community or maintainers to discuss/decide on a more appropriate and comprehensive license. A good summary of popular licenses is available [here](https://tldrlegal.com/). Some of the more popular licenses are listed [here](https://tldrlegal.com/verified) (scroll down). An alternative listing of popular licenses is available [here](http://choosealicense.com/licenses/).

body: I don't think this is an intentional feature?  I've seen it happen a number of times (Alpha version), possibly just when trying to skip back more than one jump in quick succession.

title: Option to auto download oldest episodes first

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Auto download always downloads newest episodes first. So, if the episode cache size is smaller than the number of unplayed items, older episodes are never downloaded.
Another problem is that if there are multiple new episodes from the same feed, the newer episodes end up at the top of the queue, while the other way around would make more sense.
Of course I can manually reorder the queue, but it would be nice if the order of new episodes was retained automatically.

title: Queue centric AutoDownload and Cleanup Algorithms
body:
There's been some confusion recently about when things get auto downloaded and when they get cleaned up.

Part of this is from actual bugs and part of it is because the functionality is just plain confusing.  The problem is that changing the behavior may break some users' workflows.  Some might say that those users' workflows should be broken, but it's probably wiser to find a solution that can make everyone happy.

To do that I'd like to propose a new workflow that will likely become the default, but give users the choice to retain the old one.
## AutoDownload and Queuing

AutoDownload will download and add to the queue all items which are 'New' and have auto-download enabled (e.g. it will still support disabling downloads for individual feeds).  

It currently downloads any unread items.

An item is new if it hasn't been acted on in some way.  All new items show up in 'New Episodes' currently.  This essentially makes New Episodes the list of items that will be downloaded the next time auto download is activated.

While we think we have #1009 under control with the auto-download flag, this change would certainly have helped with it too.
## Cleanup

Cleanup will consider any item that isn't currently in the queue as eligible for deletion.  Currently an item has to be fully played and not in the queue for it to be deleted.  Items won't get deleted immediately, but the next time AntennaPod needs space it will remove items that aren't queued.  This will resolve the problem of having new items but them not being downloaded because you simply removed an item you didn't care about from the queue.  Currently to make room for an item you have to mark the item as read and remove it from the queue, or go to 'Downloads' and remove it there.  Which is more complicated than needs to be.

This change to cleanup should resolve #939, #699.
## Enhancements

Some users like to keep episodes after they've already listened to them. We could add (either now or as a future enhancement) a 'Favorites' capability (something that's been requested a number of other times). Items that are 'favorited' won't be deleted by the cleanup algorithm.  (#538, wouldn't quite be as full featured as #851, but that would be more complicated to handle from a 'don't delete this' standpoint and take more time to implement)

We might want to update what makes an item appear new. With this system an item added to the queue will never be new. A user might want to be able to see what new things have been downloaded and added the queue.  Not sure what would be a good way to indicate that.

Finally, we might want to add some ability to remove stale items from the queue. User can ask to bulk remove everything older than 7 days or something to that effect.
## Transition

I think the user should be allowed to choose between this and the 'classic' algorithm, but I would like this to be the default in the future since I think it makes far more sense.  So there's a question of how to transition without having people that would prefer classic lose all their episodes.  I'd propose the following (though I'm not sure it's the best idea).

For new installs, we just default to this new algorithm.  But, if the user is upgrading, on the first launch of the app we ask the user if they want to switch to the queue centric model that allows for easier management of automatic downloads and easier cleanup of old episodes.  If they prefer they can stick with classic which downloads more things and requires more interaction to clean up old episodes.
## Implementation

We'd create a new EpisodeCleanupAlgorithm and a new AutomaticDownloadAlgorithm. Choosing the new mode would use those algorithms instead of APCleanupAlgorithm and APDownloadAlgorithm.
## Thoughts

Any thoughts or opinions?  Any other related issues I missed?

title: FeedMediaSizeService is overactive

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Currently it tries to download the size for every item, even if we already have the size.

There are a couple of reasons:
- getFeedMediaUnknownSizeCursor() should check if KEY_SIZE <= 0, but it checks > Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is everything
- Some servers always return 0 for this query, so we'll just always ask how big they are:
  (example showing some logging that has been added)

```
07-19 21:59:31.030: D/FeedMediaSizeService(21038): Getting size currently 0 for https://my.slate.com/subscriptions/media/3c83...........mp3
07-19 21:59:31.466: D/FeedMediaSizeService(21038): Size now: 0
```
- It should probably only check on sizes if isDownloadAllowed(), not just if networkAvailable().

title: Feature request: an option to change playback speed
body:
An option to change playback speed to a lower (when listening to foreign language or otherwise difficult podcasts) or higher (easy listening) setting would be very appreciated.

This could probably be integrated in the interface by adding a button on the right of the playback controls in the player view, which would trigger a pop-up menu with available speeds, Youtube-style, or a separate pop-up with a slider.

However, a brief search reveals that the Android API by default does not include a functionality to change playback speed. See [this Android issue](https://code.google.com/p/android/issues/detail?id=1961) and also [this SO question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5149050/changing-the-speed-of-music-playback-in-android). So this FR will probably have to sit here for quite a while, unless someone decides to re-implement variable playback rate, or Google suddenly releases an update.

I might have been mistaken though, as I am poorly familiar with the details of Android development, so someone should look into whether this is actually impossible with the current API.

title: Option to sort feeds alphabetically
body:
As discussed in #441 

The feeds were changed from alphabetical to number of unplayed episodes. Is it possible to make it an option?

The two ways I use antennapod are affected by this:
1. Listening to podcasts on demand: me or a friend have a specific feed that we want to listen to, so we want to pull up the feed, see if there are any new episodes or old episodes that we haven't listened to.
2. Queuing up a small percentage of subscribed podcasts.  

I know some other people personally who are the same way.  Detail from my previous post:

I have a limited amount of time available to listen to podcasts compared to the amount of subjects and podcasts I'm interested in. Most of my feeds have a large amount of unplayed new episodes, but that tag is still useful to me:
1. Subscribe to a large list of podcasts of various subjects (from educational to comedy to career-specific)
2. Select a small amount of feeds to auto-download 
3. Add specific episodes to the queue (or for direct streaming) via description
4. Let queue auto-download when on wifi

Step 3 is of course what is affected by this:
- "New Episodes" tab
  - mixes all the topics together
  - low-frequency feeds can get lost amongst higher-frequency feeds.
- Static alphabetical view of podcast feeds
  - allows quick access by subject or feed
  - tagging may work as well as I saw in another thread, but one feed may be lighthearted or heavy on the same subject, where selecting individual feeds is still useful to me
  - Unplayed tag still useful (in case marking all as read sorts it alphabetically)
    - old unplayed podcasts are useful if I've exhausted my queue for that subject

I'm open to suggestions in a better process for the same use case with the update.

As the setting depends on your use case (which doesn't usually change), it should not be on the main UI, but rather somewhere in the settings, where I personally don't think it would be considered clutter.

We send the GpodnetEpisodeAction PLAY when items are marked as read. At least we do in some when the user users the menu item to mark something as 'Played'.

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug

body:
This was reported for 1.2 and 1.3alpha.  It appears to be happening because of [this line](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/2d4705461c00dcb131b848789fa2a8a6021d19da/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/adapter/DefaultActionButtonCallback.java#L104).

I think that we actually don't want to use Gpodder in this case. The user is never actually given a choice in this view to mark an episode with media as played. So this really shouldn't be present.  This mark as 'read' is really only for website only entries. labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
I would welcome a feature to stream podcasts to dlna/upnp media renderers (cf. #280). I have implemented a proof of concept for such afeature using the cling library. (Personally, I don't consume any video podcasts and I didn't not care about them in my current implementation.) It took me a while from the first attempt, so my implementation is based on a somewhat outdated version of AntennaPod. I encourage you to have a look at it: https://github.com/volhol/AntennaPod/tree/streammedia

On the MediaplayerActivity you can find a new Item in the menu called select media renderer. 

![menu](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11587858/8340733/92a87240-1ac0-11e5-9dad-64fe018aba4a.PNG)

The app tries to find all suitable medai renderers in your local network. Just select one. The app then attemps to play the current media item form the current position on the chosen media renderer.

![select media renderer](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11587858/8340740/9c055b14-1ac0-11e5-96f0-ee32210acc74.PNG)

In fact, the app does currently not stream the content to the device itself. Instead it transmits the original URL to the device and asks it to stream the content from there. It may take a while before you can start playback. During this time, you see that the play/pause button changes appearance. Sometimes you may have to press the play button two to three time before the playback starts. Once the media item is played back on the media renderer, you can change the current position as well as the volume like you would in local mode. (Altering the volume works from the MediaplayerActivity only.)  The fast torward/reqind button disapppear since there is no suitable feature for this in dlna/upnp.

I have tested this feature on the four dlna/upnp media renderers I have access to. I found out that each of them behaves a bit differently. Thus, it may not work properly on your devices.

I am of course open to any discussion on if and how this feature could be integrated with an AntennaPod release (standard feature, separate module as prestissimo, ...). I tried to isolate most changes in separate files. Please be aware that the cling library (http://4thline.org/projects/cling/) requires at least API 15.

title: Does not add the podcast if the connection fails (OPML import)

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Hi

Maybe it makes sense to not to add a podcast, but the thing is there could be temporary connection issues with the podcast providers. 

Here is a scenario. I have 60 podcasts in an opml file. I import it and some of them fail during import and APod does not add them. They are not listed. Well what if the connection issue is temporary from the server? Sometimes the providers might get hit with lots of request which disables their response?

I think that it will make more sense if APod adds the all the podcasts during import but show some icon or gray it out next to the listing (not in downloads window) to show that it failed during the import. And maybe it will come back during another refresh.

It is a bit confusing this way because hard to keep track of which ones made it back whioch ones are not.

title: Icons missing
body:
Hi

I explained what happened with https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/951. Now I reversed back to the original path to get my episode order properly. Well problems do not stop there. I am missing all the icons. I even deleted the images and refreshed APod(which redownloaded all the images), however that does not seem to help with gaining icons back. No shows no episodes have icons.

title: Backup episodes
body:
Hi

It can be beneficial if we have a way to backup episodes functionality. By backup I do not min zipping or taring.  That way one can keep the data folder lean if there is an intention to save some epiusodes for later listening.

Basically the user will define a backup folder from the settings. And then the user can backup an episode from the episode window function menu by clicking on backup. When the user clicks on backup, APod moves the episode from the data folder to backup folder with the same folder setup like thenameoftheshow-thenameoftheepisode.mp3

thanks

title: Deleting episodes from the queue menu
body:
Hi

It would be nice if we are able to delete episodes right from the list views intsead of gong into the details of the episodes and do it that way. It is a bit convoluted to do it that way if you will.

title: Moving data folder with the whole content to a new place does not work.

labels.name: Type: Feature request

body:
Hi

Due to storage limitations I had to move my data folder from internal to an sdcard. I copied the whole structrure as is to the sdcard. I then chose the new path in the settings. Now Apod does not like to play all the downloaded episodes, it shows the episodes to be downloaded (the ones in the que which had been downloaded already). I now have to redownload all my 150 shows that are in the que. The files are there, it should not be downloading them. I have like 6.5 gb of useless (in APod) downloaded episodes now ;( 

It shows a play icon next to the downloaded ones but clicking on the icon does not play them. I open the episode, the it shows the episode to be downloaded or streamed which was not the case before I moved my folder.

I am on Android 4.4.4 CM 11

thanks

title: Play with another app
body:
Hi

This is a feature request for being able to play episodes with external apps that are installed on the system. For example my preferred player is Aimp for offline media. This kind of media passing is pretty common in other apps like file managers, media managers etc.

I do not mean to recommend a replacement replacement player, I am merely asking as a way to "share" the location of the media on the disk to another local player when the user wants.

thanks

Hi

If I wanted to implement continuous playback by default - NOT VIA THE QUEUE. User selects the latest podcast and plays it, when done it moves to the next item what would be the easiest way to do this?

Any ideas?

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
Using Lollipop (5.1.1) on a Nexus 4. I encounter the following issue:
When I change the time settings for rewind and/or forward, the settings aren't saved. 
If I use another app or even go into another part of AntennaPod and go back the buttons are back to the default setting (30s).

title: Episode necromancy

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
AP keeps resurrecting (downloading and adding to the queue) episodes I have listened to.

The resurrected episodes get added as new ones come out in the same feed. At one point the queue was completely empty, the next day I had the new episodes released that day, plus the previous one for each of those feeds. I have auto refresh on every 4th hour, along with autodowload/queue. 

When long-pressing on the episodes I have the option to mark them as unplayed, so I'm assuming AP remembers I've listened to them, or marked them as played/skipped (difference?) before. Marking then as unplayed gives me the option to play them. All the files exist on the device and I can play them immediately and I don't have the option to stream them.

When I notice this, I have to go into each episode, tap to remove the file, wait for the file to be removed, tap to remove it from the queue, back out, wait a while until the episode disappears from the queue (takes several seconds, if it even works), and hope they don't come back again.
Sorting the queue while doing this can get really interesting as it randomly ressurrects episodes I just removed too.

I have a Samsung S3 GT-I9300 with Cyanogenmod 12.1 and I'm currently in the alpha/beta program.

title: Remove button to Flattr AntennaPod

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Now that AntennaPod isn't being maintained by @danieloeh any longer and a team of people are working on it, Daniel, mentioned that he felt we should change who the Flattr money goes to.

After discussing with Daniel and @mfietz we decided that we should remove the ability to flattr the app.  The reason being that since the team is split up, there's no one person who the money should go to.  At the moment we have no expenses (apart from time).  So there really isn't a great way to deal with the revenue Flattr was providing.

We are, of course, very pleased that people like the app enough to donate.  We just don't know how to deal with those funds justly, and as a result felt it would be better to remove the ability to Flattr AntennaPod directly.

This should resolve #507 and #567 as we just won't support accepting money any longer.  If people have a better idea of what to do, please share it here.

body:
The most recent release of AntennaPod seems to have a bug that has been fixed.  Last December I reported incorrect dates on a podcast in issue #545, this was fixed correctly when the issue was closed.  With the newest release I am seen the exact same failure mode as was reported in that issue.

_It is the podcast for "[Richard Herring's Leicester Square Theatre Podcast](http://feeds.feedburner.com/RichardHerringLSTPodcast)".  Every time I add the feed it thinks every podcast is today.  The next day when I updated the feed it increments the day and shows every podcast as today._

title: Misbehaviour at end of playback when next in Queue is undownloaded

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
If you play a podcast in the Queue and the next item in the Queue is not downloaded, when the playback ends the playback controls view doesn't go away if it was open, instead just showing playback controls that don't do anything and no cover.
Furthermore, the bottom Now Playing/Play-pause bar shows the episode that just finished with the pause button.

How to replicate:
1. Put downloaded podcast in Queue
2. Put not downloaded podcast in Queue right below the previous one
3. Play first podcast
4. Go to playback controls and drag playback timer to end of file
5. Playback controls are blank (problem part 1)
6. Go back to Queue
7. Bottom bar shows just finished podcast (problem part 2)

title: Item Removed / Undo message at end of last podcast in Queue
body:
When the podcast at the bottom of the Queue finishes playing, a message appears at the bottom saying "Item Removed           Undo" where pressing the Undo returns the podcast to the Queue. 
This only happens for the bottom Queue item, perhaps because for the others there is always a bar with play button for the next episode at the bottom.
Either this message should be removed entirely, or appear consistently at the end of every podcast, right now it seems like a built-in feature accidentally left on.

How to replicate:
1. Add podcast to Queue
2. Play it
3. Go to playback controls and drag time to end of podcast
4. AP goes back to Queue and shows "Item Removed" message.

title: Parts of some episodes not deleted

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
While exploring the antennapod/files/media folder using ES File Explorer, I noticed some episodes that appeared to be still there which I had listened to and according to AP weren't there anymore.
I checked the release dates of those episodes and the 'last modified' date in the properties of these files, and the last modified date is probably the date of when I listened to it.
The file size displayed in the properties was also really small, and when trying to play the files it only plays for a little while before stopping.

What I think is going on is that when AP deletes a finished episode, it sometimes is interrupted somehow and part of the file remains. AP randomly crashes sometimes, so maybe that's when it gets interrupted? I have no idea how to replicate this but maybe keeping a list of files to be deleted and checking afterwards if they indeed are would work.

Edit: The files and dates, though I'm pretty sure it's nothing specific about these files or dates.
Release date    Podcast/episode                 Last modified date
2  feb      Hello Internet #30                  2015/05/25 16:47:54

title: Some remarks on the version released on 16.06.2015 (performance issues)
body:
Hi, I'm no contributer to AntennaPod, but simply a single user observing some issues with the newest version of AntennaPod. The update was done automatically within my Wiko Rainbow (Android 4.4.2) at 16.06.

First of all thank you for this marvellous piece of software. I'm that glad to have it as no other podcast-player on Android is that simple, minimalistic, stable and focused.

With the newest update from 16.06.2015 I observe a significant delay in displaying the episodes-lists, the played list, the podcasts themselves, etc.
The feature showing the unlistened episodes on the right side of the podcasts is great, however it looks like all the changes have changed the speed of the application overall.

Showing the playing list with 321 entries needs more than 20 seconds. Potentially a problem with the length of the list as after deletion of the playing list things are fine again.

However adding a podcast-episode to the playing list by using the context menu lasts ~10-15 seconds.

Opening a podcast-overview lasts 2-3 seconds. That's definitely longer than before. Not dramatic, but new.

But the most significant problem I observed first today having no internet connection at all. I have downloaded all the episodes and placed them in the playing list. Opening the playing list lasted approx. 40-50 seconds. Jumping back and opening one of the podcasts directly was not possible, no episodes were displayed. From my perspective AntennaPod seems to unusable if there's no internet connection even the episodes are downloaded. I could not observe this behaviour with the previously installed version.

Perhaps you can use these details for further improvement. With a heavy heart I will have to search for another podcast-player.

Ciao, Georg

title: Any ideas for AntennaPod 1.3?

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Now that 1.2 is released it's time to start thinking about 1.3.

There have been some suggestions for major UI improvements. Some visible, some under the covers.  I think it would make sense to think through all the GUI related features and changes we want and try to make them all work well together.

Some thoughts on improvements:
- Material design overhaul
- ~~Use of RecyclerView in place of DSLV~~
- New subscription view (#848, #836)
- ~~Better sharing of episodes (#861)~~
- Display of itunes 'explicit' tags (#724)
- Filtering by itunes 'explicit' tags (#725)
- ~~Support for multiple queues~~
  - I don't think this will happen in 1.3
- ~~Improve visibility of adding podcasts via iTunes~~ - Done
  - This is really the easiest way of adding podcasts
  - Perhaps making it the first option users see and only labeling it 'search'?
- ~~Download all episodes from a feed (#871, #520)~~
- ~~Episode forward/back (#732)~~

I bet there are some other good thoughts on what could be done. 

We should think hard about any changes to how we interact with the app, how these features would change them and how they could all work together.

title: Merge 1.1.2 change in to develop
body: 1.1.2 fixed a problem with the gpodder.net certificate handling for 2.3 devices. We should merge that change in to 1.2.  There will likely be a merge conflict when dealing with AndroidManifest.xml and about.html. We should probably just take the version of those files that are in develop.

title: Storage quota on data folder

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
It would be great if a could put a quota in GB on the data folder.
Therefore, if the storage space of all the downloaded episodes reach over this limit, the oldest ones will be deleted.

title: Option to set all episodes older than 'n' to be deleted.

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body: I would really like to see an option in AntennaPod to be able to set that all episodes older than 'n' days should be deleted. It could either be a sliding scale, or something like "one week", "two weeks", "one month", six months" or "one year". It would of course be even better if you could set this on a per subscribed podcast basis.

title: widget incorrectly displays information when podcast episode ends
body:
There appears to be a small issue with the widget that when the current listening episode ends all the information updates for the next podcast except the time.

What you get:

```
podcast-new title
podcast-old time played / time total
```

In the case of the time played and time total they are the same, eg 30:00 / 30:00

What you should get

```
podcast-new title
podcast-new time played / time total
```

In the case of the time played and time total they are the same, eg 00:00 / 30:00

title: 'Search' displays in toolbar as word and not icon

labels.name: Type: Confirmed bug
labels.description: Bugs confirmed by a lead developer

body:
When the search button is displayed in the toolbar it is sometimes displayed as the word 'search' instead of the search icon (the magnifying glass).

This happened on 2.3.7 in the New Episodes view when that view was empty (no new episodes). May occur at other times.

title: Auto-update at a specific time of day

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body: At the moment AntennaPod allows you to specify an update interval, x number of hours, if auto update is enable. Could we get an option to specify a time of day that updates happen.

title: Show unlistened episode count
body:
I would like suggest a new feature that would show the number un-listened to or partially listened to episodes of each posdcast that you are subscribed to.

This could be shown in the side menu next to or on top of the Podcast image.

Best example of this implementation is doggcatcher [here](https://lh6.ggpht.com/Eri_eDwfRwvWLaEJTnUfowLAMEcbN7WWHsph1MDOgG5oSu3y_UqOcUmhHFXrpDjY2A=h900) with all podcasts showing unlistened to episodes and "The Month Podcast" also showing the in progress episodes

title: Hide finished / not downloaded episodes
body:
It would be good when viewing the episode list of an individual podcast if there way a way to
1. hide completed/finished episodes
2. hide episodes not downloaded

title: Mark as unplayed
body: Would it be possible to get an option to mark episodes of podcasts as new/unlplayed if they get accidentally played.  At the moment the only way to reset the play status appears to be to play the podcast, pause it and manually scrub back to the start (00:00 time)

title: Player pauses at midnight
body:
The player pauses a playing podcasts right at midnight, observed in timezone UTC+1, from May 1st to May 2nd.
Manually resuming the player worked fine.

Version 1.1.1, via F-Droid, on Nexus 5, Android 5.1

title: make downloaded media files world-readable

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
otherwise prestissimo has no access to files created by AntennaPod

This issue is comes to light when media is stored on a filesystem that obeys file permissions.  At the moment downloaded files are readable only for AntennaPod UID.

If you point me to the right place in code where completed downloads can be processed, I'll supply push request.

title: Support syncing with TT-RSS
body:
I use [Tiny-Tiny RSS](https://tt-rss.org/redmine/projects/tt-rss/wiki) (a.k.a. TT-RSS) to manage my RSS feeds, including podcasts, but I generally prefer to use it as a backend for applications like [Liferea](http://lzone.de/liferea/) on the desktop, which use TT-RSS's [API](https://tt-rss.org/redmine/projects/tt-rss/wiki/JsonApiReference) to sync feeds.

It'd be great if Antennapod could sync with TT-RSS similarly to the way it works with gpodder.net, with the ability to specify a particular folder/category within the TT-RSS tree as the root for podcasts and have new subscriptions added within Antennapod placed there, read/unread status updated as appropriate, etc.

title: Automatic download problem
body:
I tested (months ago) the WiFi Filter. I activated the filter and added my home and work wifi. 
But I changed my mind and deactivated the filter (home and work remained with an checkmark, but grayed out) . 
Now I found out the automatic downloads does not work on other wifi than both selected.

title: Add repeat single episode option

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body: That would be useful for language learning podcasts.

title: Toggle option to have episodes deleted when swiped off the queue.
body:
Hi,

I would like to see a toggle option to have episodes deleted when swiped off the queue regardless of whether they are listened to or not. If that's not feasible a context menu option to delete the episode in addition to moving it up and remove it from the queue would be helpful.

The way I use AntennaPod keeps me in the queue most of the time. That is where I play from (thank you for including direct playback from the queue) and organize my listening, so it would be great if I could delete episodes from there also.

title: Bring user to ItemListView when subscribing to a podcast

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
I've been thinking that we have a bad user experience when you first subscribe to a podcast. Namely, you subscribe and then have to click back like 4 times to get to the main screen. It would be nice if when you subscribe it takes you to the subscribed podcast view (ItemListFragment), and then you don't have to navigate all those back buttons. 

This should make it much easier for people to interact with the podcast they just subscribed to.

title: Use different icons for "syncing" and "sync finished" notification

labels.name: Type: Feature request
labels.description: Issues which request the introduction of a new feature or improvement/enhancement of an existing one

body:
Sometimes when your connection is slow and you want to see which podcasts the app downloads. So you can decide if you want to stop the download.

On devices with bigger screens it can be annoying to open the notification area for nothing....
